significance: A three-tiered apsidal temple in Kasaragod district whose woodwork carries scenes of Ganesha and the Ramayana; the linga is said to have been found by a woman named Madaru of the Tulu Moger community, and the Ganapathi figure drawn on the sanctum wall by a boy grew to overshadow the older dedication. It was long held by the Kumbla rajas of Maipady Palace before passing to the Devaswom board.
story: Tipu Sultan is said to have come to demolish the temple but to have changed his mind after drinking water from its well, leaving only a sword mark on the well house.

name: Tali Shiva Temple
significance: One of the oldest temples of Kozhikode, built in the fourteenth century by the Zamorin and closely bound to his court; its two-storeyed sanctum is shaped like a chariot. Damaged during Tipu Sultan's eighteenth-century invasion, it was renovated in 1964.
story: The linga in the sanctum is said to have been installed by Parasurama at the close of the Dvapara Yuga.

name: Viswanatha Swamy Temple
significance: An early fifteenth-century Shiva temple on the bank of the Kalpathy river, endowed by Ittikombi Achan of the Palakkad royal family in an inscription of Malayalam Era 600 (1424-25) and ringed by four Tamil Brahmin agraharams. Its likeness to the Kashi Viswanatha temple at Varanasi earned it the name Dakshina Kashi, and it is the centre of the annual Kalpathi Ratholsavam.
story: Lakshmi Ammal of Kollengode is remembered as having carried a Shiva linga home from Varanasi and installed it here with the Raja of Palakkad's support, endowing 1,320 gold coins for its upkeep.

name: Aluva Mahadeva Temple
significance: A temple on the sand bank of the Periyar at Aluva, counted among Kerala's 108 Shiva shrines and unusual in having no sreekovil: the linga rises directly from the riverbed sand, which is why the Sivaratri gathering on the Aluva Manalpuram is held in the open.
story: Folklore holds that the sage Parashurama installed the image here.

name: Bhaktavatsala Perumal Temple
significance: A Divya Desam of the Chennai region built in the 9th-century Pallava period, its earliest inscriptions dated between 820 and 890 CE, with medieval Chola and Vijayanagara additions. It is glorified in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham.
story: The town's name, 'the place where the Lord stood', recalls the belief that Lakshmi and Vishnu descended and stayed at this spot.

name: Vimala Temple
deity: Vimala (Bimala), the tantric form of Lakshmi
dynasty: Eastern Ganga (also attributed to Somavamshi Yayati Keshari)
significance: The goddess shrine inside the Jagannath Temple complex at Puri, dated to the 9th century and built in four-part Kalinga form. It is a Shakta pitha and the ritual heart of Tantric worship within an otherwise Vaishnava sanctuary.
story: Parvati complained to Vishnu that she had lost her rightful share of offerings, and he promised she would dwell at Puri as Vimala and receive the remnants of Jagannath's food in the Kali Yuga.

name: Naimisharanya
significance: A sacred forest tract at Nimsar in Sitapur district, named repeatedly in the Puranas and in both epics. Tradition holds that the Puranas were first recited here to an assembly of sages, and the site remains an active pilgrimage centre.
story: The Varaha Purana explains the name by saying that a host of daityas was destroyed here within a single nimisha, an instant.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple
dynasty: Gwalior State (Scindia); built by Seth Gokul Das Parikh
significance: A Pushtimarg temple of 1814 in the old city of Mathura, raised by the Gwalior treasurer Seth Gokul Das Parikh with the approval of Daulatrao Scindia. It is among the busiest shrines in the town.

name: Mata Mansa Devi Mandir
style: Painted shrine complex; the 1840 Patiala Shivalaya carries 38 wall-painting panels
significance: A complex of three shrines in the Shivalik foothills of Panchkula district, built by the ruler of Mani Majra in the early 19th century and extended by Patiala in 1840. Millions of pilgrims visit during the spring and autumn Navaratras.

name: Mahavira Jain Temple, Osian
significance: Built in 783 CE under the Gurjara-Pratihara king Vatsaraja, this is described as the oldest surviving Jain temple in western India and an important tirtha, especially for the Oswal and Maheshwari communities.
story: Jain tradition holds that miracles worked by Acharya Ratnaprabhasuri converted the villagers of Osian, after which the goddess Chamunda became the temple's guardian deity.

name: Parsurameswara Temple
style: Early Kalinga Nagara, with vimana and jagamohana
significance: The best preserved specimen of an early Odia temple, raised in the mid-7th century by the Shailodbhavas, whose family deity was Shiva. It was the first here to set a jagamohana in front of the sanctum, a plan that every later Kalinga temple followed.
story: The temple's name is traced to the penance of Parashurama and the grace Shiva granted him.

name: Thiru Aadanoor Temple (Andalakkum Aiyan Perumal)
deity: Andalakkum Aiyan Perumal (Vishnu), with Ranganayaki Thayar
significance: A small Vishnu temple in the Kaveri delta a couple of kilometres from Swamimalai, counted among the 108 Divya Desams and sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. It has a three-tier rajagopuram and a Pranava vimana, and is administered by the Ahobila Mutt in the Vadakalai tradition.
story: Legend holds that Vishnu came as an old man to the riverbank and handed out sand that turned to gems for the labourers a wealthy devotee's workmen had cheated, exposing the fraud.

name: Irattai Thiruppathy (Thirutholaivillimangalam)
significance: Two adjoining Vishnu temples on the Thamiraparani that together count as the single Divya Desam of Thirutholaivillimangalam, and belong to the Nava Tirupati group strung along the Tirunelveli–Tiruchendur route. Both shrines are praised in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, notably by Nammalvar; their inscriptions name rulers between 1190 and 1345.
story: A sage named Suprabha is said to have turned up a balance and a bow while ploughing here; the objects became a human couple whom Kubera had cursed, and the place took its name from them.

name: Yogadhyan Badri Temple
significance: One of the seven Sapta Badri shrines of the Garhwal Himalaya, holding a life-size Shaligram image of Vishnu seated in meditation — the posture that gives the shrine its name. When the Badrinath temple closes for the winter its festival image is carried down to this sanctuary and worshipped here until the summer reopening.
story: Pandu, father of the Pandavas, is said to have meditated on Vishnu at this spot to be cleansed of the sin of killing two mating deer.

name: Dhyan Badri Temple
significance: One of the seven Sapta Badri shrines, standing in the Urgam valley close to Kalpeshwar on the banks of the Kalpa Ganga. Its image of Vishnu is a four-armed black-stone figure in a meditative posture, from which the shrine takes its name.
story: The shrine is credited to Urvarishi, son of King Puranjaya, who is said to have meditated in the Urgam region and founded it for Vishnu.

name: Sambisari Temple
significance: A ninth-century Shaiva temple compound that lay buried about five metres deep under Merapi volcanic deposits until a farmer struck its carved stone in 1966; excavation and reconstruction were completed in 1987, leaving the shrine sitting in a sunken courtyard.

name: Pura Luhur Batukaru
significance: One of Bali's Sad Kahyangan Jagad or six great directional sanctuaries, guarding the west and tied to the ancestors of the rajas of Tabanan; destroyed in 1604 and rebuilt in 1959, its principal shrine is a seven-tiered meru to Mahadewa on the slope of Bali's second-highest volcano.

name: Pura Dalem Sakenan
significance: A Balinese Hindu temple on Serangan island south of Denpasar, credited to the priest Mpu Kuturan and enlarged by villagers in 1982; its Kuningan-season festival draws pilgrims from across southern Bali, and the island was joined to the mainland by reclamation in 1996.

name: Kidal Temple
deity: Shiva, in the portrait form of the deified king Anusapati
significance: A slender East Javanese candi of about 1248 built as the mortuary shrine of the Singhasari king Anusapati, whose image is thought to have stood in its chamber as Shiva; its base carries three Javanese masks and reliefs of the Garuda story, and it was restored in the 1990s.

name: Sri Mariamman Temple, Medan
significance: Medan's oldest Hindu temple, raised in 1884 in the Kampung Madras quarter by Tamil labourers brought to the plantations of North Sumatra, and rededicated for Hindu Dharma worship in 1991; its gopuram makes it the focus of Thaipusam and Deepavali in the city.

name: Pura Kehen
deity: Hyang Api, the god of fire
significance: The royal temple of the Bangli kingdom, standing in terraces up a hillside with an eleven-tiered meru and a padmasana for Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva; copper-plate inscriptions from the 9th to 13th centuries mention it, and royal officials once swore their oaths of office here.
story: Villagers read the sacred banyan in the outer courtyard as an omen: a branch falling to the north-east foretells a king's death, one to the north-west a brahmin's.

name: Chau Say Tevoda
significance: A mid-12th-century Angkorian temple just east of Angkor Thom, begun under Suryavarman II with later work by Yasovarman II and Jayavarman VIII; it collapsed into some 4,000 scattered blocks and was rebuilt by a Chinese restoration team between 2000 and 2009.

name: Adichikkavu Sree Durga Devi Kshetram
significance: One of the older shrines of Pandanad village in central Travancore, dedicated to Vana Durga and managed by the Pandanad Karayogam; its sreekovil is built open at the top, the form prescribed for a forest Durga.

name: Halasuru Someshwara Temple
builtDisplay: 16th c. Vijayanagara work on a Chola-period shrine
significance: The oldest surviving temple in Bengaluru, traced to the Chola period and largely rebuilt under the late Vijayanagara Empire by the Yelahanka chief Kempe Gowda II; excavation at the site has uncovered a tank thought to be some 1,200 years old.
story: A local chief is said to have been told by Someshwara in a dream to build the temple with a hoard of buried treasure the god pointed him to.

name: Amirthakadeswarar Temple, Sakkottai
significance: A Shaiva temple near Kumbakonam sung in the 7th-century Tevaram and so counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams, built by the Cholas in the 9th century and expanded by the Thanjavur Nayaks; it is linked to Sakya Nayanar, one of the sixty-three Saiva saints.
story: In the deluge the essence of creation is said to have come to rest here in a pot of nectar, which gave the place its old name Kalayanallur.

name: Gopinath Temple, Gopeshwar
significance: An old Shiva temple at Gopeshwar in Garhwal whose courtyard holds a five-metre trident of eight metals dated to the 12th century and inscribed in the name of Ashokchalla; broken images scattered around it suggest several more shrines once stood on the site.
story: The trident is said to be the one Shiva hurled at Kamadeva, which struck the ground here and stuck fast, and is believed to quiver at a true devotee's touch though no force can shift it.

name: Kadakkal Devi Temple
significance: A goddess shrine in eastern Kollam district unusual for having neither an idol nor a priest of the ordinary kind; the village around it was a centre of social-reform agitation in the decades before Indian independence.
story: The Devi is said to have come from Tamil Nadu with four sisters and to have killed a trader named Panayappan who had cheated her family, then settled into his wooden shop, which became the sanctum.

name: Kalarickal Manikanda Swami Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Thrikkodithanam in Kottayam district that also holds the tomb of Kalarickal Gurunathan, remembered as a master of kalari payattu who served the local ruler.

name: Gorakhnath Math
significance: The head monastery of the Nath sampradaya, spread over some 52 acres at Gorakhpur on the spot where Gorakshanath is held to have practised; the city takes its name from the saint, and the math has long been a centre of the order's religious and public life.
story: A lamp called the Divya Jyoti is said to have burned in the math without interruption since Gorakshanath's own time.

name: Jatashankar
significance: A natural cave shrine north of Pachmarhi in the Satpura hills where stalagmites are venerated as self-formed lingams, fed by two springs whose pools run notably cold and warm.
story: The cave is said to be where Shiva hid himself from the fury of the demon Bhasmasura; the name joins jata, matted hair, with Shankara.

name: Alappancode Easwara Kala Bhoothathan Temple
deity: Easwara Kala Bhoothathan, a form of Shiva, worshipped with Ayyappan and Bhadrakali
significance: A pilgrimage centre in the Malayalam-speaking belt of Kanyakumari district, run by a hereditary trust, where Easwara Kala Bhoothathan is worshipped alongside Ayyappan and Bhadrakali.

name: Alattiyur Hanuman Temple
significance: A temple near Tirur whose presiding deity is Rama but which is known throughout Kerala for its Hanuman shrine; held in trust successively by the Alathiyur Nambudiris, the rulers of Vettathunad and the Zamorin of Kozhikode, it is now the leading temple of the Malabar Devaswom Board.
story: The image shows Rama giving Hanuman his instructions before the search for Sita in Lanka, with Hanuman leaning in to listen and Lakshmana standing apart so as not to overhear.

name: Iringole Kavu
deity: Durga, worshipped as Saraswati at dawn, Vana Durga at noon and Bhadrakali at night
significance: A goddess temple set inside a surviving sacred grove near Perumbavoor, counted among the 108 Durga temples traditionally ascribed to Parasurama; long held by local families, it now comes under the Travancore Devaswom Board.
story: The infant girl Kamsa seized in place of Krishna, an incarnation of Yoga-Nidra, is said to have slipped from his grasp into the air and settled in this forest as the goddess of the grove.

name: Jagdish Temple, Udaipur
significance: The largest temple in Udaipur, completed in 1651 by Maharana Jagat Singh I beside the city palace and in continuous worship ever since; a flight of thirty-two marble steps past a brass Garuda leads to the black-stone image of Jagannath under a 79-foot spire.

name: Harshnath Temple
significance: A hilltop Shaiva temple on Harshagiri about 14 km from Sikar, finished in 956 CE under the Chahamana king Vigraharaja I and endowed by the Pashupata teacher Allata from donated funds. A 973 CE inscription describes the hill as Shiva's earthly counterpart to Mount Kailasa, and the shrine drew gifts from merchants working the regional trade routes.

name: Kadu Malleshwara Temple
significance: A 17th-century Shiva temple in the Malleshwaram district of Bengaluru, built in 1669 by Venkoji, step-brother of the Maratha king Shivaji, and giving the surrounding locality its name. Shivaratri draws thousands of worshippers from across the city.

name: Ghanteswara Siva Temple
significance: A small Shaiva shrine standing inside the Kapileswara temple precinct in Bhubaneswar, built in the Kalinga manner with a three-tiered pidha vimana on a triratha plan and rising only about 2.8 metres.

name: Gupteswar Cave
significance: A limestone cave shrine about 55 km from Jeypore in Koraput district, housing a two-metre Shiva lingam that devotees believe is still growing. Worship was formally established in the mid-17th century by Maharajah Veer Vikram Dev, and Mahashivaratri now brings more than two hundred thousand pilgrims up its two hundred steps.
story: Rama is said to have found the hidden lingam while crossing the Dandakaranya forest with Sita and Lakshmana and named it Gupteshwar, the god in hiding, after which it lay forgotten until a hunter stumbled on it again.

name: Ammachiveedu Murti Temple
significance: A goddess temple at Thangassery in Kollam district founded in the 15th century by the Ammachiveedu family, with the present building completed in 1968. The deity has no image: she is worshipped as two gold-clad conches on a silver-covered peedam inside a four-foot-square sanctum, and the shrine is open to worshippers of any caste or faith.
story: Oral tradition holds that a Brahmin patriarch of Parappur married a woman born under an ill-omened star, and that the deity was moved into a conch at Sasthamcotta with the instruction to found her worship wherever a tree should split open.

name: Jagannath Temple, Alwar
significance: A Vishnu temple in Alwar whose sanctum is unusual in holding two Jagannath images at once, one fixed and one movable, alongside Sitaram and Janki. Its walls and pillars carry uncommon floral motifs, and its ritual calendar differs from the Puri tradition.

name: Hanuman Garhi Temple
deity: Hanuman (in his child form on Anjani's lap)
significance: One of Ayodhya's principal shrines, reached by seventy-six steps and laid out like a four-sided fort with round bastions at its corners and a silver-worked sanctum. It is administered by the Bairagi mahants of the Ramanandi sampradaya and the Nirvani Akhara.
story: Hanuman is said to have taken up residence in a cave on this spot to keep watch over Ramkot after Rama returned to Ayodhya from his victory over Ravana.

name: Radha Damodar Temple, Vrindavan
significance: Founded in Vrindavan in 1542 by Jiva Goswami, this is one of the central shrines of Gaudiya Vaishnavism and preserves the Giriraj Shila, a Govardhan stone kept as a relic within the temple.
story: The Giriraj Shila is said to carry Krishna's own footprints and to have been handed to Sanatana Goswami by Krishna himself, so that four turns around the temple are held to equal one circuit of Govardhan Hill.

name: Gokarnanatheshwara Temple
significance: Built at Kudroli in Mangalore in 1912 by the Billava leader Koragappa and consecrated by the social reformer Narayana Guru, who brought its Shiva lingam himself, the temple was founded so that the Billava community could worship on its own terms. A 1991 rebuilding in Chola style added a sixty-foot gopuram, and the temple hosts the city's Mangalore Dasara.

name: Aisanyesvara Siva Temple
significance: A 13th-century grey sandstone shrine on a saptaratha plan in the Old Town of Bhubaneswar, close to the western wall of the Lingaraja temple. It remains in worship, and the processional image of Lingaraja is brought here on the sixth day after Shivaratri.

name: Aluvamkudi Sree Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Gurunathanmannu in Pathanamthitta district that lay abandoned until a hunter came upon it in the 1940s. Worship was restored and is now held on the first day of every Malayalam month, with Shivaratri as the yearly festival.
story: The shrine is held to have been established by Parashurama, and local tradition says Rama performed worship at the spot.

name: Agasteeswarar Temple, Kolapakkam
significance: A Shiva temple at Kolapakkam on the western edge of Chennai, whose complex also holds shrines to the Navagrahas, the nine planetary deities.
story: The sage Agastya is said to have worshipped Shiva here, and the presiding deity takes his name from it.

name: Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Gadhada
significance: One of the six temples raised by Swaminarayan himself, opened on 9 October 1828 in the courtyard of Dada Khachar's residence at Gadhada on land the family donated. The two-storey, three-domed shrine stands on a raised plinth with an assembly hall, pilgrim lodgings and kitchens, and in 2012 became the first temple in Gujarat to receive golden spires.

name: Guru Narasimha Temple, Saligrama
significance: A Vaishnava temple at Saligrama, 22 km from Udupi, whose two-armed lion-headed image of Narasimha is carved from saligrama stone and dated to the 8th century. The Kota Brahmins of fourteen surrounding villages take this deity, rather than any human acharya, as their sole guru.
story: The deity is said to have appeared of its own accord at the foot of a pipal tree, holding conch and discus.

name: Kaliyuga Varadaraja Perumal Temple
deity: Vishnu (worshipped as Kambamperumal, a granite pillar)
significance: A Vishnu temple at Kallankurichi near Ariyalur, roughly five centuries old, unusual in that the presiding deity is not an image but a twelve-foot granite pillar known as Kambamperumal. Its Vijayanagara-period ardha mandapam carries sculpted pillars illustrating Vaishnava narratives.
story: A cowherd named Maangan is said to have found a pregnant cow beside a sacred pillar here and, directed by Vishnu, to have raised a temple around it.

name: Kalahastiswamy Temple, Uthamapalayam
significance: A Shiva temple at Uthamapalayam in Tamil Nadu notable for its wall paintings, which date to the Madurai Nayak period.
story: The shrine is said to have been built jointly by three rulers who had been at war with one another and settled their quarrel by raising it together.

name: Kalikadevi Temple
significance: A sandstone pidha deul at Kancha Sahi in the Old Town of Bhubaneswar, enshrining a four-armed goddess worshipped locally as Kali. Its dry-masonry construction places it in the 10th or 11th century, earlier than the local attribution to the Somavamsi kings, and it remains in private hands and active worship.

name: Bhandara Ghara Shrine
significance: A 16th-century shrine within the Kapileswara temple precinct at Bhubaneswar, built with a pidha-order vimana. It holds the chalanti pratima, the movable images of Vishnu and Shiva carried out in procession at festival times.

name: Laddu Baba Temple
significance: A medieval Shiva temple at Sharanakula in Nayagarh district that blends Kalinga and Dravidian forms and is a focus of Shaiva worship in southern Odisha. Unusually for a Hindu temple, its priesthood has long been drawn from lower castes; Mahashivaratri is its main festival.

name: Dashabhuja Ganapati Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple at Erandwane on Karve Road in Pune, once held by Haripant Phadke, a sardar of the Peshwas, and later given to the Peshwas as dowry. Its image is prized for a trunk turning to the right, a form regarded as rarer and more sacred, and the shrine draws large crowds through Ganesh Chaturthi.

name: Dimapur Kalibari
significance: A Kali temple completed in 1956 in Dimapur, serving as a centre of Hindu worship in Nagaland and observing Durga Puja and Kali Puja as its principal festivals.

name: Lakshmi Narasimha Temple, Bhadravati
deity: Lakshmi Narasimha (with Venugopala and Vishnu Purushottama)
significance: A soapstone trikuta temple at Bhadravati built around 1250 under the Hoysala ruler Vira Someshwara, with three sanctums and star-shaped outer walls that Adam Hardy singles out as among the finest stellate work of the dynasty. Its reliefs range across Vaishnava, Shaiva, Shakta and Vedic subjects, and it is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Daksheswar Mahadev Temple
significance: A Shaiva temple at Kankhal, about four km from Haridwar, raised in 1810 by Queen Dhankaur of the Landaura estate and rebuilt in 1962. The complex takes in a Das Mahavidya shrine, a Ganga temple and the Daksha Ghat on the river.
story: Hindu tradition places King Daksha's sacrifice here: slighted by his exclusion from it, Shiva's wife Sati threw herself into the fire, whereupon Shiva sent Virabhadra and Bhadrakali to behead Daksha, who was later restored to life with a goat's head.

name: Bhringesvara Siva Temple
significance: An 8th-century light grey sandstone shrine at Khatuapada on the south-eastern edge of Bhubaneswar, built as a pancharatha rekha vimana on a raised platform some 26 metres long. It stands west-facing in the Dhauli foothills beside the Daya river and is now protected by Odisha State Archaeology.

name: Dirgheshwari Temple
significance: A Shakta pitha on a rocky hill in North Guwahati, built in brick between 1714 and 1744 under the Ahom king Siva Singha with Tarun Duwarah Barphukan overseeing the work. Its sanctum lies underground inside a natural cave, and the shrine, recognised by the Archaeological Survey of India, is held locally to be second in sanctity only to Kamakhya.
story: A limb of Sati is said to have fallen here after Vishnu's discus scattered her body, and the sage Markandeya is remembered as having won Durga's blessing through penance at the spot.

name: Kunnuvarankottai Kasi Visalakshi-Viswanathar Temple
significance: A Shaiva temple near Batlagundu in Dindigul district, roughly five centuries old, modelled on the Visalakshi-Viswanathar shrine at Varanasi and distinctive for its south-facing sanctum of the goddess. It is linked to Sacchidananda Bharati I, the 25th acharya of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham, who was born nearby and whose birthday is kept here each year; consecrations were held in 2001 and 2013.
story: Local tradition holds that the image was carried here from Kasi by a devotee.

name: Dhabaleswar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on an island in the Mahanadi about 27 km from Cuttack, raised in the 10th century under the Somavamshi king Yayati Keshari and later repaired by the rulers of Athgarh. It is reached by boat or by Odisha's first hanging footbridge, and draws crowds at Shivaratri and the Bada-osha fair.
story: The name is explained by a tale in which Shiva turned a black calf white to shield a thief who had taken refuge with him, dhabala meaning white.

name: Dishisvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva (lingam in a circular yoni pitha)
significance: A 15th-century laterite shrine built by dry masonry in Khurda district near Bhubaneswar, standing inside a private compound. Vegetation over the superstructure and cracks in its roof have left it dilapidated despite repairs by the state archaeology department.

name: Bhadra Maruti Temple
significance: A Hanuman temple at Khuldabad, about 4 km from the Ellora caves, rebuilt in white marble in the 1960s after the earlier shrine was destroyed under Mughal rule. It is one of only three known temples where Hanuman is shown sleeping, the others being at Prayagraj and Jam Sawali, and fills with pilgrims at Hanuman Jayanti and Ram Navami.
story: Hanuman is said to have fallen into bhava-samadhi here while listening to King Bhadrasena sing in praise of Rama, and to have agreed at the king's request to stay on and bless those who came.

name: Bhoothalingaswamy Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Boothapandi in Kanyakumari district, traditionally credited to the Pandya king Pasum Pon Pandyan in the first century CE. It has a temple tank, the Theppakulam, and observes a car festival with processions of its deities.

name: Bhagabati Temple, Banapur
significance: A goddess temple at Banapur in Khordha district, counted among the Shakta pithas of Odisha and reckoned to be about seven centuries old. Banapur was the seat of the Sailodbhava dynasty, and Buddhist images found in the town also connect the place with the Vajrayana tradition.

name: Lankeswari Temple
significance: A Shakta shrine standing within the bed of the Mahanadi at Sonepur, whose goddess was the presiding deity of the region once known as Paschima Lanka. It is maintained in worship by the Kaibarta community of Sonepur and the wider Subarnapur district.

name: Kuttumuck Siva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple about 5 km north-east of Thrissur where the god is worshipped in the fierce Kiratha form, with subsidiary shrines to Ganapathy, Ayyappan and Vishnu. Its image is reputed to be more than three centuries old, though no records survive to confirm it; the ten-day Utsavam Pallivetta ending in the Aarattu is its chief festival.
story: When Tipu Sultan's Mysore army advanced on the temple, a swarm of bees is said to have risen and driven the soldiers back.

name: Lankeshwar Temple
significance: An old hilltop Shiva shrine in western Guwahati near the Gauhati University campus, held by Shaivites to be among the most sacred in the city and visited by pilgrims and tourists alike through the year.

name: Tirucherai Saranathan Temple
builtDisplay: 10th c. (Chola); later Vijayanagara and Nayak work
significance: One of the 108 Divya Desams, praised in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham and carrying inscriptions of the Chola king Parakesari Varman (906–946 CE), with later building by the Vijayanagara rulers and the Madurai Nayaks. Its granite-walled enclosure runs 380 feet on each side behind a five-tier, 120-foot gopuram, and it is the only Divya Desam where Vishnu has five consorts and the river Kaveri has a shrine of her own.
story: Vishnu is said to have appeared as a child to the river goddess Kaveri while she did penance to be reckoned the equal of the Ganges, showing her all ten of his avatars and granting her precedence during the month of Tula.

name: Laxmi Narayan Temple
significance: A small Vaishnava shrine of about 3.2 metres inside the Kapileswara temple precinct at Bhubaneswar, built with a pidha-order vimana. Its image shows Lakshmi and Narayana seated in padmasana on a lotus pedestal, with a Garuda pillar set before the entrance.

name: Labesvara Siva Temple
significance: A 15th-century sandstone Shiva temple at Bhubaneswar, locally also known as Hanumantesvara. The fabric has weathered badly, with rainwater entering the sanctum through cracks in the roof.

name: Beleswar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on the coast of Puri district in Odisha, standing beside the sea beach that takes its name from the shrine.

name: Dakshina Mookambika Temple, North Paravur
significance: A goddess temple at North Paravur in Ernakulam district whose sanctum stands within a lotus pool, with subsidiary shrines to Ganapathy, Kartikeya, Vishnu, Hanuman and others. It is best known for Navaratri, when a music festival is held and children are initiated into letters at the Vidyarambham on Vijayadashami.
story: The ruler of Paravur, who travelled each year to the Mookambika temple at Kollur, is said to have been told by the goddess in a dream to make her image near his palace so that he could see her daily.

name: Dhari Devi Temple
deity: Dhari Devi, a form of Kali
significance: A Shakta shrine on the Alaknanda at Kalyasaur between Srinagar and Pauri Garhwal, counted among the 108 Shakta pithas and revered as the guardian deity of Uttarakhand and of the Char Dham pilgrimage. No record survives of when the first temple was raised; the image was moved on 16 June 2013 for a hydroelectric project, hours before the floods that devastated the region.
story: Dhari Devi is said to have been the youngest of seven children, killed by her brothers on an astrologer's warning and thrown into the river, her upper half coming to rest at Kalyasaur and her lower half at Kalimath.

name: Bhima Devi Temple Complex
significance: The remains of a Gurjara-Pratihara temple complex at Pinjore in Panchkula district, built between the 8th and 12th centuries on a panchayatana plan of a main shrine ringed by four subsidiary ones, comparable to work at Khajuraho and Bhubaneswar. Its sculpture spans Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta subjects, and the site is now an open-air museum beside the 17th-century Yadavindra Gardens.
story: The Devi Mahatmya tells of Bhimadevi manifesting in colossal form in the western Himalaya near this place to protect the sages.

name: Chittoor Sree Krishnaswamy Temple
significance: A 13th-century Krishna temple at South Chittoor near Ernakulam, founded by the Cheranelloor Swaroopam, with a square sanctum under a copper-plated pyramidal roof in the Kerala manner. It has been administered by the Cochin Devaswom Board since independence.
story: A young member of the founding family, Narayanan Kartha, is said to have dreamed that Krishna promised to travel with him inside an umbrella and to settle wherever it was set down, and the temple was raised on that spot.

name: Bhairabi Temple
significance: A Shakta shrine at Kolibari near Tezpur overlooking the Brahmaputra and the Kolia Bhomora bridge, where Bhairavi is venerated as one of the Mahavidyas. Its stone carvings have been dated to the 9th century, and the structure has suffered earthquake damage.
story: Local tradition holds that Usha, daughter of the asura king Banasura, came regularly to this spot to worship the goddess.

name: Bhattarika Temple
significance: A riverside Shakti shrine on the bank of the Mahanadi at Sasanga in Baramba, Cuttack district, where the goddess Bhattarika is worshipped as a manifestation of Durga. Durga Puja is its principal annual observance.
story: Puranic tradition says the goddess appeared at this spot to lend Parashurama her power when he faced defeat at the hands of Sahasrarjuna.

name: Bhuvaneshwar Temple, Boudh
significance: A tenth-century Shiva temple at Malipara in Boudh town, on the right bank of the Mahanadi, raised under Somavamsi rule. Its walls carry khakhara-mundis and carved figures that include Ganesha alongside Jaina Tirthankaras.

name: Bhalei Mata Temple
builtDisplay: built by Raja Pratap Singh; date unrecorded
significance: A hill shrine in Bhalei village, Chamba district, built by Raja Pratap Singh and later renovated by Raja Sri Singh, whose sanctum holds a two-foot black stone image of the goddess. It draws large pilgrim gatherings at the Ashwin and Chait Navratris; the image was stolen in 1973 and recovered near Chohra.
story: The goddess is said to have appeared to Raja Pratap Singh in a dream asking to be brought out of a hidden place called Bhran, and the palanquin carrying her would move no further than Bhalei, which was read as her choice of site.

name: Cuttack Chandi Temple
significance: A Shakti shrine near the bank of the Mahanadi in Cuttack, dedicated to the goddess Chandi and counted among Odisha's principal goddess temples.

name: Bijasan Mata Temple
significance: A hilltop Devi temple on the edge of Indore, built in 1760 by Shivaji Rao Holkar and overlooking the city's airport. It draws thousands of pilgrims through Navaratri.

name: Biranchinarayan Temple, Palia
significance: A thirteenth-century sun temple at Palia in Bhadrak district, reconstructed in the early twentieth century by a local zamindar. Its sanctum holds a four-faced stone Surya image on a seven-horse chariot, and its eastern doorjambs appear to be reused from a 10th-11th century Shaiva temple.

name: Bhadrakali Temple, Aharapada
significance: A Shakti temple at Aharapada, some 8 km southwest of Bhadrak town, whose black granite goddess is seated in lotus posture on a lion.
story: Tradition holds that the image was first worshipped by the sage Tapasa Rushi in a cave on Meghasana hill in Mayurbhanj, and was carried to Aharapada by his disciples to keep it safe from Kalapahad.

name: Kurungaleeswarar Temple
significance: A medieval Shiva temple at Koyambedu on the bank of the Cooum in Chennai, dated to the twelfth-century Chola period and enclosing a large tank. The goddess is worshipped here as Dharmasamvardhini, and the temple tree is a jackfruit.
story: The shrine is said to have been developed by the sage Valmiki while Sita lived there after her separation from Rama, and is remembered as a place of family reunion after Rama was reunited with Lava and Kusha.

name: Lakshmi Narasimhar Temple, Narasinghapuram
significance: A Vaishnava temple at Narasingapuram in Tiruvallur district that preserves fourteen inscriptions, twelve of them Vijayanagara, recording patronage by Achyuta Deva Raya in the 1530s and endowments as late as 1608. Its earliest records date to Kulothunga Chola I and Vikrama Chola.

name: Lakshminarasimha Temple, Haranhalli
significance: A three-shrined Hoysala temple at Haranhalli in Hassan district, completed in the 1230s at the expense of three brothers and now a protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India. Its shrines house Venugopala, Keshava and Lakshminarasimha; originally dedicated to Kesava, it was later renamed for Lakshminarasimha.

name: Ganga Jadadisvarar Temple
significance: A Chola Shiva temple at Govindaputtur on the north bank of the Kollidam, built in 980 CE under Uttama Chola through his officer Ambalavan Paluvur Nakkan. It is counted among the Vaippu Sthalams and is praised in the Tevaram hymns of Appar and Sambandar.

name: Elai Kaatha Amman Temple
significance: A village goddess temple at Koyil Patti in the Kurichipatti panchayat of Madurai district, about 14 km from Melur, known chiefly for its annual festival cycle.
story: Local tradition treats Ezhai Kaatha Amman and the deity Valladikaarar as sister and brother, and their festivals are kept in relation to each other.

name: Madayi Kavu
significance: A hilltop Bhadrakali kavu at Madayi near Pazhayangadi in Kannur district, with four sanctums and worship in the Kaula tradition performed by Pidarar Brahmins. During Hyder Ali's incursion of 1780 the Nair warrior Vengayil Chathukutty is recorded as having defended it from desecration; it is now under the Malabar Devaswom Board.
story: The goddess is said to have slain the demon Darika, after which Shiva directed Parashurama to establish her shrine on this hill.

name: Ekambareswarar Temple, Chennai
significance: A Shiva temple on Mint Street in George Town, Chennai, built in the 1680s by Alanganatha Pillai, a dubash to the British East India Company. It appears on a 1710 map of Madras as 'Allingall's Pagoda' and stands among the Jain shrines and the Kandaswami temple of the same street.

name: Mahadeva Temple, Kalanjoor
significance: A Shiva temple at Kalanjoor in Pathanamthitta district, recorded as at least 1,100 years old, which carries the unusual feature of two adjacent copper-clad flagstaffs because both Mahadeva and Sastha are enshrined. Its 60-foot gopuram is approached by eighteen steps, and it lies about 80 km southwest of Sabarimala.

name: Elamgulam Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
builtDisplay: deity held to be c. 800 years old; renovated 2023
significance: A Sastha temple at Elamgulam in Kottayam district whose written history begins with its management by the Edappally royal family; control passed from the Nair Service Society to a wider committee in 1978. A major rebuilding in stone, wood and copper was completed in January 2023, and its annual Gajamela brings out some fifteen elephants.

name: Nedumpura Kulasekharanellur Shiva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, at Nedumpura in Thrissur district, distinguished by a sanctum built in the Gajaprishta form of an elephant's back. Krishna, Ganesha and Sastha are enshrined as subordinate deities.

name: Maa Bhangayani Temple, Haripurdhar
significance: A goddess temple at Haripurdhar in the Lesser Himalayan foothills of Sirmaur district, and one of the district's principal pilgrimage sites; it stays open to visitors year-round.
story: Tradition holds that Maa Bhangayani gave her blessing to Shirgul Maharaj, through which the king of Bagad and Guga Peer secured his release from Mughal captivity.

name: Iranikulam Mahadeva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, near Mala in Thrissur district, unusual in having two main shrines whose Shiva forms are worshipped as Thekkedathappan and Vadakkedathappan. Parvati and Subramanya are enshrined in the northern shrine.
story: The shrine is traditionally said to have been consecrated by the sage Parashurama.

name: Gajanan Maharaj Temple, Indore
significance: A temple to the Shegaon saint Gajanan Maharaj in Paliwal Nagar, Indore, begun in 1988 on land donated by Mr. Paliwal and completed in 1994 in Dholpur stone and marble. Its octagonal sanctum stands for the eight siddhis attributed to the saint, and the Thursday Mahaprasad, begun in 1992 with thirteen devotees, remains its central weekly rite.

name: Kottappuram Siva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Poothole in Thrissur, close to the Vadakkunnathan temple, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. Maha Shivaratri is its principal festival.
story: The temple is traditionally said to have been installed by the sage Parashurama.

name: Chakkamkulangara Siva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala named in the Shivalaya Stotram, standing north of the Poornathrayeesa temple in Thrippunithura, the old Brahmin settlement that served as the Cochin kingdom's capital. It is unusual in also carrying a full Navagraha installation.
story: The lingam is traditionally said to have been installed by the sage Parashurama.

name: Eravikulangara Temple
significance: A temple at Akaparambu in Ernakulam district where the Devi is the principal deity alongside Shiva and Sastha. A Thambula Prasna held in 2007 led to the installation of Brahmarakshas and Naga shrines the following year.
story: The goddess is said to owe her strength to the Brahmachari scholar Sankara Sarma, who moved his household worship of Bhadrakali to this temple before renouncing the world.

name: Maa Simsa Temple
significance: A shrine to Sharada Devi at Simsa village in the Ladbharol area of Joginder Nagar subdivision, Mandi district, drawing its largest gatherings at Navratri; a second temple to the same goddess stands at Daroh near Palampur.

name: Durga Mandir, Ramnagar
significance: A square stone Durga temple at Ramnagar, Varanasi, raised by Maharaja Balwant Singh of Banaras. Much of it was destroyed by British cannon fire when Warren Hastings sent troops to seize Raja Chait Singh, and it was afterwards rebuilt to the original design; it remains under the Banaras royal family.
story: The shrine is said to have been dedicated to Vishnu at first and turned over to Durga after unexplained happenings in its compound.

name: Lodheshwar Mahadev Mandir
significance: A Shiva temple on the bank of the Ghaghra at Mahadeva village in Barabanki district, whose lingam is reckoned among the rarest of the 52 associated with the Shakti Pithas. It is the kuldevta shrine of the Lodhi Rajputs, and a well beside it is known as the Pandav-Kup.
story: Tradition says that when Parashurama was destroying the kshatriyas, the surviving Lodhis appealed to their deity, who told them to lay down weapons and take up the tools of agriculture.

name: Durga Devi Temple, Guhagar
significance: A Durga temple in the coastal town of Guhagar, Ratnagiri district, laid out on the panchayatana plan with four corner shrines around the central sanctum, and set beside a tank with a wooden pillar at its centre.
story: The goddess is said to have destroyed the forces menacing Guhagar and slain the demon Mahishasura, and is worshipped here as Mahishasuramardini.

name: Mahadeva Temple, Avittathur
significance: A Shiva temple at Avittathur in Thrissur district, counted among the sixty-four ancient Brahmin settlements of Kerala and protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. The Avittathur inscription of AD 1024 records grants of paddy land for its upkeep under the Cheras.
story: The lingam is traditionally said to have been installed by Parashurama, with the sage Agastya laying out the temple and fixing its daily rites.

name: Malayalappuzha Devi Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali temple at Malayalappuzha in Pathanamthitta district whose 5.5-foot image is made in katu-sarkara-yogam and shows the goddess in her fierce form; the sanctum holds three images, used respectively for worship, abhisheka and sreebali. Its consecration is credited to the Aikireth and Eravimangalath Namboothiri families, and its eleven-day festival opens on Thiruvathira in Kumbham.
story: Two Namboothiri pilgrims are said to have been directed by Bhadrakali herself to enshrine her at Malayalappuzha as the most auspicious place.

name: Garh Ganesh Temple
significance: A hill temple on the Aravalli ridge above Jaipur, founded by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, the city's founder, in connection with an Ashvamedha yajna. Its Ganesha is shown without a trunk, an uncommon form, and the shrine is reached by 365 steps standing for the days of the year.

name: Durga Temple, Motia
significance: A tenth-century Kalinga temple near Krushnaprasad in Cuttack district whose four-armed goddess is shown slaying Mahishasura with conch and discus in her upper hands. Sculptures recovered from the site by the Archaeological Survey of India place its origin in the Somavamsi period, with eight-armed Durga pieces comparable to those at the Vaital temple.

name: Eri-Katha Ramar Temple
significance: One of the oldest Rama temples in South India, at Maduranthakam in Chengalpattu district, counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of Vaishnavism and endowed by the Chola king Parantaka I. Ramanuja is held to have received his Pancha Samskaram here beneath the temple's magizha tree.
story: The temple's name is traced to 1798, when the British Collector Lionel Blaze is said to have seen Rama and Lakshmana standing as warriors on the bunds of the tank as it threatened to breach in the monsoon.

name: Durga Temple, Baideshwar
significance: An eighth-century shrine at Baideshwar in Cuttack district built as a khakhara vimana in the early Kalinga manner, comparable to the Vaital Deula and the Varahi Deula at Chaurasi. Besides the eight-armed Durga it houses images of Parvati, Aja-Ekapada Bhairava and Ganesha.

name: Duladeo Temple
significance: The last of the Chandela temples at Khajuraho, standing by the Khodar river and dedicated to Shiva, whose name means 'holy bridegroom'. It is a nirandhara temple on the seven-chariot plan, one of the twenty-two Shiva shrines of the group inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

name: Ganapati Temple, Redi
builtDisplay: shrine raised after the idol's discovery in 1976
significance: A Ganesha shrine at Redi in coastal Maharashtra, about 30 km from Vengurla, built around an image dug out of the shore near Rewati port in 1976. The idol stands roughly 6 ft high and is dwibhuja, two-armed rather than the usual four; the mouse that serves as his vahana was found two months later.
story: A local man, Sadashiv Kambli, is said to have seen the buried Ganesha in a dream and persuaded villagers to dig it out of the seashore.

name: Gajanan Maharaj Temple, Kanhor
significance: A temple to the Shegaon saint Gajanan Maharaj at Kanhor in Kulgaon-Badlapur, Thane district, opened on Vijaya Dashami in 1981 on land given free by Vitthalrao Raut. Its Seva Samiti dates from the same year and has kept the Prakat Din Utsav annually since.
story: The temple is said to have been begun after the devotee Shripadrao Kulkarni was directed to it in a dream, and an audumbar tree that sprang up beside the chosen site was taken as a sign.

name: Garbharakshambigai Temple
deity: Shiva as Mullaivananathar, with Parvati as Garbharakshambigai
significance: A Shiva temple at Thirukarukavur in Thanjavur district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams sung in the Tevaram and one of the five Pancha Aranya forest shrines of the Kumbakonam country. Thirty-one inscriptions record land grants by Rajaraja I, Rajendra Chola I and Kulothunga Chola.
story: The goddess is said to have shielded a pregnant woman's unborn child in a pot after an angry sage cursed it, which is why she is invoked as the protector of the womb.

name: Rangnath Dol
significance: An Ahom-period Shiva temple raised in 1703 on the bank of the Joysagar tank near the Talatal Ghar, built under the Ahom king Sukhrungphaa (Rudra Singha). It remains an active place of worship and an example of early 18th-century Assamese temple building.

name: Jharkhand Dham
significance: A Shaiva pilgrimage cluster of about ten shrines near Dhanwar in Giridih district, centred on a Shiva temple that draws an annual fair. A Sanskrit college, the Sanskrit Hindi Vidyapith, was founded at the site in 1967.

name: Sarada Mutt, Sivagiri
significance: The shrine to Sarada Devi on Sivagiri hill, founded by the social reformer Sree Narayana Guru, whose foundation was laid in 1909 and consecration completed in 1912. Its octagonal plan with windows and ventilation broke with tantric temple convention, and worship there is by hymn rather than by food offering or ritual anointment.

name: Narasimha Swamy Temple, Seebi
significance: A late 18th-century Dravidian temple to Narasimha built over roughly a decade by three brothers, sons of Kacheri Krishnappa, a Dewan under Tipu Sultan. It has a three-tiered gopura, a prakara wall and open and closed mantapas.
story: B. Lewis Rice records that a merchant's pot of grain turned blood-red when boiled on a sacred rock here, and that the god appeared in his dream asking that a temple be raised in atonement.

name: Ramapuram Devi Temple
significance: Described as one of the older and more important temples of the Travancore region, it served as the kingdom goddess temple of the Odanadu rulers. Its congregation spans three karas of Ramapuram village, and its festivals follow the Malayalam calendar dates of Vrishchika Bharani, Kumbha Bharani and Makara Ashwathi.

name: Veeranarayana Temple, Gadag
style: Chalukyan with Hoysala and Vijayanagara additions
significance: An 11th-century Vishnu temple of the Chalukyas of Kalyani, thoroughly renovated under the Vijayanagara empire, so that its inner mantapa, garuda stambha and gopura represent three successive building traditions. An inscription of c. 1539 records a gift to the temple in the reign of Achyuta Deva Raya.
story: The Kannada poet Kumara Vyasa is said to have composed his Mahabharata at a particular pillar in this temple, inspired by the deity.

name: Mulavana Mahadevar Temple
significance: The principal temple of Mulavana and its neighbouring villages, with subsidiary shrines to Sastha, Ganapathi, Yakshiyamma and Nagaraja. Hereditary management rested with the Kadalayi Mana family before passing to the Mulavana Mahadevar Devaswom.

name: Arakeshwara Temple, Haleyedatore
builtDisplay: present complex early 19th c. (Wodeyar); 12th c. origin
significance: A Shiva temple on the Kaveri whose origins go back to the era of Kulottunga Chola I, with the present Dravidian complex - gopura and pillared mukhamantapa - endowed by Maharaja Krishnaraja Wodeyar III according to B. Lewis Rice. It is now a protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Shivoham Shiva Temple
significance: A modern Bengaluru temple consecrated by the Shankaracharya of Sringeri in February 1995, known for a 65-foot seated Shiva murti by the sculptor Kashinath and a 32-foot Ganesha added in 2003. Renamed Shivoham Shiva Temple in 2016, it draws around half a million visitors a year.

name: Lakshmikanta Temple, Kalale
significance: A Vaishnava temple of the early 18th century enlarged by grants from the Mysore king Dodda Krishnaraja I, with a gopura and sikhara in the Dravidian manner. Records note a metallic Rama image given by the local chief Devarajiah of Kalale and silver gifts made by Tipu Sultan in 1791; it is an ASI-protected monument.

name: Saarvajanika Nagabrahmastana Moodanidambooru, Bannanje
significance: Described as one of the oldest nagabanas of Udupi district, this serpent shrine venerates Nagaraja alongside Brahma, Raktheshwari, Nandikona, Kshetrapala and the daiva Bobbarya. Its main observances are Nagara Panchami, Subrahmanya Shasti, Navaratri and the annual Varshikotsava.

name: Ramchaura Mandir
significance: A temple to Rama whose central object of worship is a pair of footprint impressions, run by the Bari Sangat monastic succession over more than twenty generations. Archaeological finds excavated at the site are held in the Patna Museum, and Rama Navami is its principal festival.
story: Local tradition holds that Rama halted here on his way to Janakpur, leaving the footprints, and that his first head-shaving ceremony was performed at the spot.

name: Maddi Anjaneya Temple
significance: A Hanuman shrine near Jangareddygudem in West Godavari district where the deity is held to be self-manifest in a sacred tree rather than housed in a conventional sanctum, so no arch surrounds it.
story: The temple's tradition tells of a demon named Madhvasura who, reborn across ages as a devotee, was saved from a lake by a monkey he recognised as Hanuman, and asked to be reborn as the tree in which the god would remain forever present.

name: Annapurna Devi Mandir
significance: Built in 1729 by the Maratha Peshwa Bajirao I beside the Kashi Vishwanath precinct, this Nagara-style temple honours the goddess of nourishment. It holds two images of the goddess, one of brass shown daily and one of gold unveiled only on Annakut day.
story: It is told that when Shiva called all the world including food mere illusion, Parvati made food vanish until he conceded its necessity, whereupon she took the form of Annapurna and set up a kitchen in Varanasi to feed her devotees.

name: Pohlani Mata Temple
significance: A hill shrine to the goddess Pohlani Mata about 8 km from Dalhousie in Chamba district, reached on a ridge that looks out over the Pir Panjal range.
story: The goddess is said to have taken the forms of a young maiden and of a wrestler in order to destroy demons.

name: Othera Puthukulangara Bhagawathi Temple
significance: One of about thirty Durga temples of central Kerala where the old Dravidian ritual art of Padayani is performed each year. It is said to be the only temple that stages the Chattathel Kolam, a figure made from 1001 areca sheaths.

name: Sri Kanaka Maha Lakshmi Temple
significance: A Devi temple in the Burujupeta quarter of Visakhapatnam and one of the most visited shrines of the city, where the image of Lakshmi is held to be swayambhu, or self-manifested.
story: The goddess is said to have severed one of her own arms, vowing to grant wealth only to the worthy and not to the ungrateful.

name: Banni Mata Temple
significance: An old goddess shrine at about 2,600 m at the foot of the Pir Panjal near Tundah village, facing the Manimahesh peak, and an important pilgrimage of the Bharmour region. Its fair falls in Bhadrapada around August and is led by a temple chela, or oracle.

name: Barfani Dham
significance: A three-tiered temple complex at Rajnandgaon that stacks distinct shrines by level - Patal Bhairavi below, Navadurga or Tripura Sundari in the middle, and Shiva with a large linga and Nandi at the top - joining Shaiva and Shakta worship in one structure.

name: Rojhri Dham
significance: A Hanuman shrine about a kilometre from Rojhri village on the Anupgarh-Bikaner road, with subsidiary temples to Shiva and Rama and walls painted with figures of gods and saints. Its largest gatherings fall on Chaitra Purnima and Ashvin Purnima.

name: Thycaud Dharma Sastha Temple
significance: A Kerala-style temple in the Thycaud quarter of Thiruvananthapuram dedicated to Dharma Sastha, a dedication comparatively uncommon even in south India. It is administered by the Nair Service Society and keeps Mandala-Makaravilakku as its main festival, with shrines to Ganapathy, Vishnu, Shiva, Durga, Hanuman and Subramanya.

name: Revansiddha Temple
significance: A 16th-century shrine to Revansiddhanath a short distance outside Renavi village in Khanapur taluka, Sangli district, said to have been raised by Shri Yogiraj Anna Sakhare and kept by the Sakhare family since.

name: Rudreswar Temple
significance: Built in 1749 by the Ahom king Pramatta Singha at the spot where his father Rudra Singha died, and named for him when the linga was installed. Its plan borrows from Mughal mausoleum design and includes underground chambers, drainage and ventilation; damaged in the 1897 and 1950 earthquakes, it is now protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Kallisseri Azhakiyakavu Devi Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali temple on the bank of the Pamba in Chengannur taluka, one of roughly thirty temples of central Travancore where the ritual art of Padayani is performed each year. The four-armed image is carved in wood, and shrines to Karimkali, Yakshiamma, Rakshassu and the naga deities stand alongside.

name: Thalappara Kotta
significance: A fortified shrine in the Goodrical forest range associated with the Sabarimala pilgrimage, whose hereditary Kochuvela chiefs still perform ritual duties through the Mandala-Makaravilakku season. Forest officials moved the structure from its old position on the Pandalam thara trek route to its present site at Plappally.
story: It is remembered as a rest station built for Manikanda on his way to Sabarimala, the Pandalam raja appointing the Thalappara chief as his guard and giving him a conch, a sword and a turban as marks of the office.

name: Thirupalkadal Sreekrishnaswamy Temple
significance: The Adikulakovil, or lineage temple, of the Ay kingdom of Kupaka, whose origins are traced to the Sangam era and which was renovated in the 9th century by the Venad king Vallabhan Kotha. Its circular sanctum houses a four-armed image of Krishna, and it is counted among the Abhimana Kshetrams.

name: Sree Rakthakanda Swamy Temple, Omalloor
significance: A temple traced to the 8th century that serves as a halt for pilgrims travelling to Sabarimala, known for its stone carvings and for a golden flagstaff raised in 1952. Its ten-day festival in Medam ends with an arattu procession to the Achenkovil river accompanied by more than ten caparisoned elephants.
story: Tradition connects the deity to the village of Kalleli near Konni, whose people are said to have cast the image into the Achenkovil river after losing at the dice game of choothu.

name: Sengazhuneer Amman Temple
significance: A coastal Amman temple at Veerampattinam, said to be about a thousand years old and the first in Puducherry to own a temple car. Its festival runs six consecutive Fridays from the Tamil month of Aadi, and the fifth Friday, a declared public holiday in Puducherry, draws well over a hundred thousand pilgrims; under French rule the Lieutenant Governor was invited to start the procession.
story: A fisherman named Veeraraghavan is said to have netted a piece of wood that bled when his wife tried to split it for firewood, after which the goddess told him in a dream to make her image from it at the spot where a cobra struck the ground three times.

name: Saptamatruka Temple
deity: Saptamatrikas (Brahmani, Vaishnavi, Indrani, Narasimhi, Chamunda, Kaumari, Varahi)
significance: A shrine to the seven mother goddesses on the south bank of the Baitarani at Jajpur, beside the Dashaswamedha Ghat and the Budha Ganesha temple, whose images are dated to the 11th century and connected with the Ashvamedha of Yayati Keshari. Long derelict, it was restored by the Archaeological Survey of India, and the goddesses are treated as attendants of Viraja.
story: The seven are said to have issued from the body of Durga as she fought the demons Shumbha and Nishumbha, each embodying the will of the god whose name she bears.

name: Gunja Narasimha Swamy Temple, Tirumakudal Narasipura
significance: A 16th-century Vaishnava temple of the Vijayanagara period at the confluence town of T. Narasipura, with a gopura over its gate and a four-pillared mantapa. It was maintained by annual grants from the Dalavoys of Mysore, repaired under the British Raj according to B. Lewis Rice, and is now an ASI-protected monument.
story: It is said locally that the place outweighs Kashi in sanctity by the weight of a single gunja berry, the berry of the tree at the temple entrance from which the deity takes his name.

name: Lal Keshwar Shiv Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Bagmusa near Hajipur in Vaishali district whose present building was completed in August 2015, housing the deity in linga form.

name: Kaal Bhairav Mandir, Varanasi
significance: The shrine of Kaal Bhairav in the Visheshwarganj quarter of Varanasi, regarded as the guardian of the city; the present structure dates from the middle of the 17th century, though the shrine itself is older.
story: Shiva is said to have created Kaal Bhairav to humble Brahma's pride, and after he struck off Brahma's fifth head he came to Varanasi, where the head fell and the spot became the Kapal Mochan Teerth, Shiva then decreeing that he remain in the city forever.

name: Someshvara Temple, Haranhalli
significance: One of the two surviving major temples of Haranhalli, completed in the 1230s by the Heggade brothers Peddanna, Sovanna and Kesanna, with a single stellate sanctum and an enclosed circumambulation path in mature Vesara form. More damaged than the neighbouring Lakshminarasimha temple, it keeps notable relief panels and is a protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Rajagopalaswamy Temple, Mannargudi
builtDisplay: Chola foundation; greatly expanded 16th c. (Thanjavur Nayak)
significance: A large Sri Vaishnava temple founded under Kulothunga Chola I and enlarged by later Cholas and above all by the Thanjavur Nayak ruler Vijayaraghava Nayak, who added the great gopuram, the thousand-pillared hall and the compound wall. Known as Dakshina Dwaraka and Champakaranya Kshetram, it counts sixteen gopurams, seven prakarams and twenty-four shrines and heads the list of 108 Abhimana Kshetras.

name: Sankata Devi Mandir
significance: Built in the late 18th century by the king of Baroda together with the Sankata Ghat below it, and held to be the only temple in India dedicated solely to Sankata Devi, the ten-armed Matrika whose name means danger. The ghat was rebuilt in stone in 1825 by the widow of a Brahmin pandit, and the goddess is honoured on the eighth day of Navratri.
story: The Pandavas are said to have worshipped Sankata Devi here during their exile.

name: Ratnagiri Murugan Temple
significance: A hilltop shrine to Murugan at Thirumanikundru in Ranipet district, attested by the 14th-century poet Arunagirinathar, in keeping with the old maxim that wherever there is a hill there is Murugan. Its principal observances are Adi Krittikai, Kanda Shashti, Navaratri and Panguni Uttiram.

name: Ranganathaswamy Temple, Bengaluru
deity: Ranganathaswamy (Vishnu) with Bhudevi and Neela Devi
significance: A 16th-century Vaikhanasa temple in the old Chickpet quarter of central Bengaluru, with carved granite pillars showing Hoysala influence. The street it stands on, Rangaswamy Temple Street, is named after it.

name: Damodar Sansthaan, Zambaulim
significance: The temple of Damodar, a form of Shiva held by the Gowda Saraswat Brahmin community, whose deity originally stood at Mathagam in old Margao where the Holy Spirit Church now is. The mahajans moved it to Zambaulim around 1565 ahead of the Portuguese temple demolitions in Salcete, the Desais of Rivona granting land and a continuing vatan for its upkeep; subsidiary deities include Chamundeshwari, Mahakali and Mahesha.

name: Madan Mohan Temple, Karauli
deity: Radha Madanmohan (Krishna with Radha and Lalita)
significance: Completed in 1600 by Gopal Singh of Karauli on the bank of the Bhadravati in the Aravalli hills, to house a Madan Mohan image brought from Vrindavan for safety. It is counted among the four dhams of Karauli district and is treated as a required halt on the Govardhan Yatra.
story: Gopal Singh is said to have been told by the deity in a dream to fetch his Madan Mohan image from Vrindavan to Rajasthan before Aurangzeb's attacks on temples.

name: Ragigudda Anjaneya Temple
significance: A Hanuman temple on a rocky knoll in Jayanagar 9th Block, Bengaluru, built in 1969 by a group of local young men and registered as a trust in 1972, and now one of the busiest shrines in south Bengaluru.
story: The hillock is said to have formed from ragi given as alms by a pious woman named Sudharma to the three great gods in disguise, who afterwards revealed themselves and turned to stone nearby, the three stones now bearing their carved figures.

name: Revanasiddeshwara Betta
significance: A Shaiva hill shrine about 15 km from Ramanagara, important to the Virashaiva tradition, which venerates Revana Siddeshwara as a reincarnation of Jagadguru Renukacharya. Three temples occupy the hill: Revanasiddeshwara at the summit at about 935 m, Bheemeshwari midway and Renukamba at the base.
story: Revana Siddeshwara is said to have emerged from the Somashekhara linga and to have practised austerities on this mountain before attaining lingaikya and passing to Kailasa.

name: Venugopalaswamy Temple, Devanahalli
significance: A Dravidian temple inside Devanahalli Fort, dated to the period after the Vijayanagara empire by a Kannada inscription of 1697 within it. Its gopura, dravida shikhara, yali pillars and carved interior columns are protected as a monument of the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Wagheshwari Temple
significance: A well-known Mumbai goddess temple in Gokuldham, Goregaon East, its entrance flanked by large elephant sculptures. Navratri is its main festival, marked by a sindoor ceremony in which married women apply the red powder to one another's foreheads.

name: Birla Mandir, Shahad
significance: A stone temple at Shahad in Thane district raised by the Birla family and dedicated to Vithoba and Rukmini, the deities of the Maharashtrian Varkari tradition. Carved figures cover its inner and outer walls, stone elephants stand at the entrances, and its setting has been used as a location in Hindi films including Suhaag of 1979.

name: Konchiravila Devi Temple
significance: A Devi temple at Konchiravila in Thiruvananthapuram district, standing at about 42 m above sea level and serving the surrounding locality.

name: Annamanada Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Annamanada counted among the 108 ancient Shiva shrines of Kerala, unusual in that Parvati and Vishnu are installed alongside Shiva with equal standing. It is administered by the Cochin Devaswom Board and keeps Maha Shivaratri as its principal festival.
story: Tradition holds that the shrine was consecrated by the sage Parashurama, and its lingam is worshipped as Kirathamurthi granting the Pashupatastra to Arjuna.

name: Kalleshwara Temple, Hire Hadagali
significance: A twin-shrine soapstone temple raised about 1057 CE by Demarasa, a minister of the Western Chalukya king Someshvara I, and enlarged by later additions recorded in Old Kannada inscriptions. It is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India as a monument of national importance.

name: Anikkattilammakshethram
deity: Shiva and Parvati (Jagat Pita and Jagat Mata)
significance: A temple on the bank of the Manimala river where Shiva and Parvati are enshrined together in a single sanctum, a pairing said to be among the rarest in Kerala. Its eight-day Pongala in the month of Kumbham draws thousands of women who cook offerings along a two-kilometre stretch around the shrine.

name: Maruthamalai Marudhachalamurthy Temple
significance: A hill temple to Murugan set on a granite outcrop about 12 km west of Coimbatore in the Western Ghats, run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department. It is popularly counted as a seventh addition to the Six Abodes of Murugan.
story: The sage Pambatti Siddhar is said to have done penance here, to whom Murugan first appeared as a serpent and then in his own form with Valli and Devasena.

name: Karingattukavu Devi Temple
significance: A goddess temple on the bank of the Pampa at Prayar in Chengannur taluk, dedicated jointly to Durga and Bhadrakali. Its annual festival falls in the Malayalam month of Meenam, with Karthika as the chief day.

name: Kovur Sundareswarar Temple
significance: A south-facing Shiva temple with a seven-tiered rajagopuram on the western edge of Chennai, counted among the city's Navagraha temples. The Carnatic composer Tyagaraja composed the five songs of the Kovur Pancharatnam here.
story: The place is said to take its name from Mahalakshmi, who came to the spot in the form of a cow to worship Shiva.

name: Kanjiramvila Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A Bhagavathy temple at Chathannoor in Kollam district that serves as both a pilgrimage centre and a local tourist draw. Its Gajamela elephant pageant is the occasion that brings the largest crowds, including foreign visitors.

name: Kottekkad Temple
significance: A village temple about 8 km from Thrissur whose sanctum holds Bhagavathi. Several further consecrations stand in the compound, among them Shiva, Hanuman, Ayyappan, Subrahmanya, the serpent deities and Brahmarakshassu.

name: Karimpuzha Sree Ramaswamy Temple
significance: A Rama temple on the bank of the Karimpuzha river in Palakkad district, historically held by the Eralpad, heir to the Zamorin of Kozhikode. It is described as one of the rare Mahakshetrams of Kerala and is known locally as Dakshina Ayodhya.
story: Local tradition identifies the Karimpuzha with the Sarayu and holds that Rama ended his earthly life in its waters, which is why Hanuman, his companion in those last moments, is enshrined within the temple.

name: Krishnaswami Temple, Muthialpet
significance: A Krishna temple in the old George Town quarter of Chennai, completed in the 18th century. It became the flashpoint of the 1787 riot between the Left-hand and Right-hand caste groupings, which the Madras Presidency authorities had to mediate.

name: Budha Ganesha Temple
significance: An 11th-century khondalite shrine near the Dasashwamedh Ghat of the Baitarani, enshrining Ganesha in an aged form. Loose sculptures of Vishnu, Mahishamardini and the Jain Tirthankara Shantinath are kept at the site, and Ganesh Chaturthi is its main festival.

name: Annakoteshvara Temple
significance: A pancharatha Shiva temple of Suryavamsi Gajapati date at Latadeipur in Dhenkanal district, combining a rekha deula with a pidha hall. It is listed as a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India.
story: The temple's lingam is said to have been dislodged during the raids of Kalapahad, the general who invaded Odisha from Bengal.

name: Kopineshwar Mandir
significance: Thane's principal Shiva temple, founded under the Shilahara dynasty and rebuilt in 1760 with further renovations in 1879 and 1996. Its lingam, about 12 feet across, is among the largest in Maharashtra, and Shiva here is treated as the patron deity of the city.

name: Apparswami Temple
deity: Apparswami (Shaivite saint), worshipped as a shivalinga
significance: A Shaivite shrine on Royapettah High Road in Chennai raised over the tomb of Apparswami, a 19th-century saint. His chief disciple Chidambaraswamy set a shivalinga above the grave, around which the temple grew.

name: Budha Deula
deity: Shiva (twin lingams on a shared yonipitha)
significance: An east-facing Shiva shrine at Badu Sahi in the old town of Bhubaneswar, holding two lingams on a single circular yonipitha plus four more recovered from the Bindusagar tank. It stands between the Bindusagar, the Mohini temple and the Akhada Chandi temple, and is used for sradha and other funerary rites.

name: Kanila Shree Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A Bhagavati temple in Manjeshwaram taluk of Kasaragod district, standing beside the coastal highway about a kilometre north of Hosangadi junction. The trust also runs an arts and culture hall and an English-medium school on the temple grounds.

name: Tiger Cave
significance: A Pallava rock-cut shrine near Mahabalipuram, its portico framed by a crown of carved tiger heads, attributed to the reign of Rajasimha Narasimhavarman II. An inscription found in the complex in 2005 led to the excavation of an older Murugan temple of Sangam date nearby; the site is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Kasi Viswanatha Temple, Ayanavaram
significance: A Shiva temple on Konnur High Road in Ayanavaram, Chennai, built during East India Company rule by the Tawker family of the city's Gujarati merchant community. It is now administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.

name: Kozha Sree Narasimhaswami Temple
significance: A Narasimha temple at Kozha near Kuravilangad, reckoned among the older shrines of Kerala and lying in territory that belonged to the Vadakkumkoor principality until about 1752. Narasimha is worshipped here in his calm aspect after the killing of Hiranyakashipu, and Narasimha Jayanti is the chief festival.
story: The image is held to be swayambhu, found in the forest by a hunter, whom some traditions identify as Shiva himself, and consecrated by the local people.

name: Koteshwar Mahadev
significance: A cave shrine to Shiva on the Alaknanda about 3 km from Rudraprayag town, at roughly 885 m. Mahashivratri is its main observance, and a 60-bed charitable hospital run by a Shankaracharya trust adjoins the temple.
story: Shiva is said to have paused to meditate in this cave on his way to Kedarnath while eluding the demon Bhasmasura, whom he later destroyed.

name: Arattupuzha Temple
significance: A Dharma Sastha temple near Thrissur under the Cochin Devaswom Board, best known for the Arattupuzha Pooram, the oldest of Kerala's pooram festivals. The pooram is styled a Devamela, the yearly gathering of the region's deities.
story: The deity is believed to carry the vital force of Vasishta, family preceptor of the Raghu line and teacher of Rama, and the temple is said to be three thousand years old.

name: Kartikeya Temple, Pehowa
significance: A Nagara-style shrine at Pehowa in Kurukshetra district, described as one of the oldest Kartikeya temples in north India. It worships the god in his celibate form, and women are barred from entering.
story: The Skanda Purana account followed here has Kartikeya born of the fire of Shiva's third eye, carried by Agni and Ganga, reared by the six Pleiades in a reed thicket and grown to six faces before slaying the demon Taraka.

name: Chammanad Devi Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali temple at Kodamthuruth near Ezhupunna, midway between Vyttila and Cherthala, held and run by the eight households of the Ettu Veettil Kartha family. Its ten-day Utsavam falls in the Malayalam month of Kumbham, and two subsidiary shrines to Sastha and Krishna belong to it.

name: Brahmani Temple
significance: A laterite pidha-vimana temple of Somavamsi date at Avana in Balasore district, pancharatha in plan, enshrining a chlorite image of Chamunda. It remains in worship and is a protected monument of the Odisha State Archaeology, its loose sculpture including a four-armed Avalokiteshvara that points to a Buddhist presence at the site.

name: Ampal Brahmapureeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Ambal in Tiruvarur district, held to be the last of the sixty raised-platform maadakoil shrines built by Kochengat Chola, with a three-tiered rajagopuram. It is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, sung by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram, and is run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.
story: Brahma, cursed by Shiva, is said to have worshipped here and bathed in the temple tank Annam Poigai to regain his form.

name: Kote Jalakantheshwara Temple
significance: A Shiva temple of Chola date near Kalasipalya in old Bangalore, renovated by Kempegowda, the city's founder. It is unusual in carrying three sanctums, to Jalakantheshwara, Parvati and Kailashnathar.

name: Kottarakkulam Sree Mahaganapathy Kovil
significance: An old Ganesha shrine in Kollam town rebuilt into its present form in 1984, also housing Nagaraja and Ayyappan. It is maintained by the roughly 270 Tamil Brahmin families of Kollam and is known for its Ashta Dravya Mahaganapathy Homam and Vinayaka Chaturthi celebrations.

name: Kapilash Temple
significance: A hill temple to Shiva as Chandrasekhar in Dhenkanal district, dated by its inscriptions to 1246 and credited to the Eastern Ganga king Narasingha Deva I. Its 60-foot tower stands at about 2,239 feet, reached by a flight of 1,352 steps, and shrines to Ganesha, Kartikeya, Ganga, Jagannath and Vishwanath share the complex.
story: The hill is identified with the ashram of the sage Kapila and is called by some a second Kailash of Shiva.

name: Asramam Sree Krishna Swamy Temple
significance: A Krishna temple on the shore of Ashtamudi Lake at Asramam in Kollam, raised on a mound of earth dug from what is now its tank. Its ten-day festival ends in the Kollam Pooram in mid-April, and the compound holds a separate Ayyappan shrine with the eighteen steps of Sabarimala.

name: Kamakshi Amman Temple, Mangadu
significance: A temple in the Chennai suburb of Mangadu where Parvati is worshipped as Tapas Kamakshi, the goddess at her penance. Its chief object of worship is an Ardhameru yantra that receives only kumkum offerings, and the seven-tiered rajagopuram is a recent addition; the temple is run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.
story: Parvati is said to have done severe penance on this spot, standing amid fire with one foot raised, to rejoin Shiva after playfully covering his eyes, and Adi Shankara is held to have installed the Ardhameru chakra to cool the heat of her austerity.

name: Chakkulathukavu Temple
significance: A Durga temple on the Pampa at Neerattupuram, about 9 km from Thiruvalla, which grew from a family shrine into one of Kerala's best-known temples. Its Pongala in the month of Vrischikam draws hundreds of thousands of women, and it also keeps the twelve-day Panthrandu Noyampu fast and the Naree Pooja.

name: Cherthala Karthyayani Devi Temple
significance: The principal temple of Cherthala, where the goddess is worshipped in an aniconic form set below ground level and held to be self-manifested. Its Cherthala Pooram is reckoned second among Kerala's poorams and is unusual for an Aarattu performed twice daily; Gandhi addressed a gathering here on 18 January 1937.
story: The saint Vilwamangalam Swamiyar is said to have consecrated the goddess at this spot on his way back from installing the deity at the Padmanabhaswamy temple in Thiruvananthapuram.

name: Budhanath Temple
significance: A Shaivite temple on the Ganga at Jogsar in Bhagalpur, counted among the 108 Nath shrines named in the Shiva Purana, with a lingam regarded as self-manifested. It draws more than a million pilgrims through the month of Shravan and is the starting point of an annual Kanwar Yatra to Basukinath.
story: Tradition places its origin in the Treta Yuga and credits its consecration to the sage Vashishtha, while the image of Bhavani in the compound is said to have floated down the Ganga from Munger.

name: Ram Mandir, Bhubaneswar
significance: A privately endowed temple near Kharavel Nagar on Janpath in Bhubaneswar, holding marble images of Rama, Sita and Lakshmana with further shrines to Hanuman and Shiva. Its tall spire is a landmark of the city, and it keeps Ram Navami, Vivaha Panchami and a Raksha Bandhan fair.

name: Kottukal Cave Temple
significance: A rock-cut shrine near Anchal in Kollam district, two chambers hewn under a single boulder with a monolithic Nandi, dated by historians to about the 7th century and credited to the ruler Nedila Paranthaka Nedumchadayan of Chadayamangalam. It is held to be contemporary with the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram and is now served by the Travancore Devaswom Board.
story: Local tradition says the great rock was carried to the spot by Shiva in his several forms, Nandi among them.

name: Kasi Viswanatha Temple, West Mambalam
significance: A 17th-century Shiva temple in West Mambalam, Chennai, named for the Vishwanatha temple at Varanasi and also called Mahabilva Kshetra. It is run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department, which conducted its kumbhabhishekam in September 2023.

name: Koothanur Maha Saraswathi Temple
significance: The only temple in Tamil Nadu with Saraswati as its presiding deity, at Koothanur in Tiruvarur district; shrines to her are rare anywhere in India. The medieval Tamil poets Ottakoothar and Kambar sang of it, and Vijayadasami is its chief festival.

name: Ananthasayana Temple
significance: A temple near Hampi raised in 1524 by Krishnadevaraya in memory of his dead son, its long rectangular sanctuary entered through triple doorways under a vaulted roof some 24 metres high. It falls within the Group of Monuments at Hampi, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1986.
