story: The image is said to have been carried here under an injunction not to look back; when the guide broke it, the figure would move no further and stayed at Holalu.

name: Anandavalleeshwaram Sri Mahadevar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Kollam city completed in the 11th century, its teak sanctum housing Shiva facing west and Parvati as Anandavally facing east. It is counted among the 108 principal Shiva temples of Kerala, and its ten-day festival falls in the month of Meenam.
story: Folklore credits the installation of the lingam here to the sage Parashurama.

name: Brahmeshvara Temple, Kikkeri
significance: A Hoysala temple at Kikkeri finished in 1171, paid for by a woman named Bammave Nayakiti in the reign of Narasimha I, and drawing Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta imagery together. Its aedicules reproduce Nagara, Dravida, Vesara, Bhumija and hybrid tower forms, and it is a protected monument of the Karnataka heritage department.
story: Village tradition holds that a tribal chief named Keeka asked a king for a settlement bearing his name, complete with temple, tank and fort.

name: Karaikal Ammaiyar Temple
deity: Karaikal Ammaiyar (Punithavathi), with Somanathar and Somanayaki
significance: A temple on Bharathiar Street in Karaikal built in 1929 by Malaiperumal Pillai for Punithavathi, known as Karaikal Ammaiyar, the foremost woman among the sixty-three Nayanmars of Saiva Siddhanta.
story: She is remembered for feeding Shiva as the mendicant Bhikshatana with curd rice and mangoes, which is why mangoes are given out at the Mangani Tirunal on the full moon of Aani.

name: Kottarakkara Sree Mahaganapathi Kshethram
significance: A Kerala temple in Kollam district whose formal presiding deity is Shiva, but where ritual precedence is given to the Ganesha (Mahaganapathi) shrine. It is widely known for its unniyappam offering and admits non-Hindu visitors.

name: Brahma Temple, Niali
significance: A rare temple dedicated to Brahma, standing near the Prachi river in Cuttack district; the present pidha-deula structure was rebuilt in the 12th century around a four-faced Brahma image of the 7th-century Shailodbhava period.
story: Local Brahmin tradition holds that Brahma himself performed an Ashwamedha sacrifice at this spot.

name: Anicad Sree Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A hilltop goddess shrine in Kottayam district where Kali is worshipped in her younger Bala Bhadrakali form, the idol installed facing east as a mirror image. Its principal observance is the Kalamezhuthupaattu held in the Malayalam month of Meenam.

name: Kamakshi Amman Temple, Saidapet
significance: A goddess temple on Chetty Street in Saidapet, Chennai, reckoned to be over three centuries old. It is administered by the Vishwakarma community and counts as one of that community's five holy shrines in Chennai district.

name: Anjaneya Temple, Nanganallur
significance: Built by the Sri Maruthi Bhaktha Samajam Trust, this Chennai temple holds a 32-foot Hanuman carved from a single granite block, among the tallest such images in India, beneath a 90-foot tower. The Kanchi seer Chandrashekarendra Saraswati installed the idol in 1989, and the state endowments department took over administration in 2013.

name: Annapurneshwari Temple, Cherukunnu
significance: One of only two Annapurna temples in Kerala, originally a Vishnu-Krishna shrine roughly 1,500 years old; the Annapurna image was installed by Avittam Thirunal Raja Raja Varma of the Chirakkal Kovilakam. Both deities occupy sanctums of equal size, and the temple was re-consecrated on 23 February 1994.
story: The goddess is said to have sailed from Kashi with two other devis in a golden ship steered by a boatman, coming ashore at the beach now called Aayiram Thengu.

name: Payammal Shatrughna Temple
significance: One of the very few Indian temples dedicated to Shatrughna, youngest of Rama's brothers. It is the fourth stop on the Nalambalam pilgrimage, made in the Malayalam month of Karkidakam.

name: Sree Indilayappan Temple
deity: Shiva (as a lingam, with Parvati and Vishnu)
significance: A temple near Kottarakkara in Kollam district, reckoned about 1,500 years old, where Shiva is worshipped as a lingam alongside Parvati and Vishnu. It admits visitors of all faiths.

name: Ravishwarar Temple
significance: A Chola-era Shiva temple in the Vyasarpadi quarter of Chennai, entered through a three-tier rajagopuram. Its sanctum is pierced by a lingam-shaped aperture that admits sunlight, and its tank is called Bhrama or Surya Theertham.
story: The sun god is said to have worshipped here and bathed in the tank to be freed of his Brahma-dosham, while the sage Vyasa's worship at the site is said to have given the neighbourhood its name.

name: Shri Pathirakali Mariamman Temple
significance: Founded from 1852 by the Nadar community of Tirumangalam, who had been barred from existing temples, and first consecrated in 1857. Its associated PKN Vidhyasala trust has run schools in Madurai district since 1908.
story: The town's name Tirumangalam is traced to a belief that the mangalyam for the goddess Meenakshi, or for Murugan's wedding, was made there.

name: Kalijai Temple
place: Kalijai Island, Chilika Lake, Khordha district
significance: A Shakta shrine on an island in Chilika Lake, recorded as built in 1717 by Jagannath Mansingh, king of Bankad (present-day Banapur). It draws large crowds at the annual Makar Sankranti fair each January.
story: The goddess is said to be Jaai, a newly married girl who drowned when her boat capsized in a cyclone while crossing Chilika to her husband's island home, and whom the lake's people afterwards venerated as a deity.

name: Rudra Mahalaya Temple
significance: Begun under the Chaulukya founder Mularaja and consecrated to Shiva by Jayasimha Siddharaja in 1140, this was one of medieval Gujarat's grandest temples. Much of it was destroyed under Ahmad Shah I and part converted into a congregational mosque; the surviving torans and pillars are an ASI Monument of National Importance.
story: Local lore says two robbers stumbled on the ancient foundations and a Shiva linga at the site, and their report of heavenly visions moved Siddharaja to complete the temple.

name: Shree Kailasha Nathar Temple, Piramanoor
deity: Shiva (as Kailasha Nathar), with Kamatchi Ambiga
significance: A Shaiva temple in Piramanoor village near Tiruppuvanam, built in Pandya style over roughly 78 cents of land with shrines to Ganesha, Murugan, Vishnu and the Navagrahas. Pradosham and Karthikai are its chief observances.
story: Brahma is said to have carried a lingam here from Mount Kailash and worshipped at the spot in penance after his dispute with Vishnu over supremacy, giving the village its name.

name: Vazhappally Maha Siva Temple
significance: Rebuilt under the Chera ruler Rajasekhara Varman in the early 9th century, this Changanassery temple issued the Vazhappally copper plate, the earliest surviving inscription in the Malayalam language. It is counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala and is unusual in having two nalambalams and two flagstaffs, with 17th-century wood carvings.
story: Tradition holds that ten Brahmin families rescued the Shiva linga from Neelamperoor and brought it here, and that Parasurama himself installed the deity.

name: Vasantha Vallabharaya Temple
significance: A Chola-period Vishnu temple at Vasanthapura on the southern edge of Bengaluru, associated with two surviving sacred springs, Devatirtha and Vasantatirtha; the others were filled in as the city grew.
story: The sage Mandavya is said to have found a self-manifested image of Vallabharaya here and raised the shrine, at the springs where the god bathed after his marriage to Lakshmi.

name: Mammiyoor Temple
deity: Shiva as Uma Maheshwara (with a Vishnu shrine)
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala and the principal of five Shiva shrines around Guruvayur; custom holds that a visit to the Guruvayur temple is incomplete without also visiting Mammiyoor. It is run by the Malabar Devaswom Board and open only to Hindus.
story: Brihaspati and Vayu are said to have found Shiva in penance at the rudratheertha here; Shiva moved aside to make room for the Vishnu idol once worshipped by Krishna, and the place came to be called Mahimayur, later Mammiyoor.

name: Dharmalinga Malai
deity: Shiva (Dharmalingeswarar), worshipped as a swayambhu lingam
significance: A hilltop Shiva shrine about 13 km south of Coimbatore, reached by a climb of nearly 800 steps. Its Chitra Pournami girivalam draws crowds in the tens of thousands.

name: ISKCON Temple, Pune
style: North Indian (red stone and marble), with a South Indian Venkateswara shrine
significance: A six-acre Gaudiya Vaishnava temple complex in Kondhwa built over seven years and inaugurated in 2013, described as the largest temple in Pune. It runs daily Bhagavad Gita and Srimad Bhagavatam classes.

name: Shri Alkheswar Mahadev Mandir
significance: A Shiva temple in Bera village, Mathura district, whose walled complex also holds shrines to Ram and Sita, Ganesha, Brahma, Durga, Radha Krishna, Shani and Hanuman beside a sacred tank. A fair is held each March and Mahashivratri draws the largest crowds.
story: The Shiva idol of the main shrine is said to have been found in the Alkheswar Kund, the pond adjoining the temple.

name: Somabaresvara Siva Temple
deity: Shiva (lingam set in a square sandstone yonipitha)
significance: A small west-facing Shiva shrine inside the Kapilesvara temple precinct at Bhubaneswar, now buried up to its baranda. Its tiered pidha superstructure is a compact example of Kalinga temple form.

name: Siddheshwar & Ratneshwar Temple
significance: A paired Shaiva temple about 2 km from Latur city, credited to the reign of King Tamradwaj. It hosts a large annual fair at Mahashivratri.

name: Bhawani Waghjai Temple, Terav
deity: Bhavani and Waghjai, with Kalkai, Navdurga and Shiva
significance: A goddess temple at Terav in Chiplun taluka, rebuilt from May 2003 on a shrine of the nineteenth century. The 123 ft hall seats about 2,000 people beneath a 55 ft dome over a 9 ft black-stone Bhavani image.

name: Sarasbaug Ganpati Temple
significance: Built in 1784 by Sawai Madhavrao Peshwa on an island in the lake laid out below Parvati Hill, this Ganesha temple is one of Pune's busiest shrines, with roughly 10,000 visitors a day rising to 80,000 at Ganesh Chaturthi.

name: Shri Katyayani Baneshwar Temple, Aversa
significance: A coastal Karnataka temple of about 1600 whose goddess is the kuladevi of Konkani Gaud Saraswat, Saraswat and Daivajnya Brahmin families and of Konkani Kharvis. Its trust now runs the temple on solar power.

name: Kundrathur Murugan Temple
significance: A hill temple on the outskirts of Chennai attributed to Kulothunga Chola II, and said to be the only Murugan shrine in Tamil Nadu where the god faces north. It is administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.
story: Murugan is said to have halted on this hill while travelling from Tiruporur to Tiruttani after defeating the demons, which is why the site is called South Thanigai.

name: Camp Hanuman Temple
significance: One of India's largest Hanuman temples, founded by Pandit Gajanan Prasad inside the Ahmedabad cantonment and long associated with army personnel. A 2021 proposal by its trustees to move it to the Sabarmati riverfront was blocked after priests and devotees petitioned the Gujarat High Court.
story: The Hanuman image enshrined here is held to be swayambhu, self-manifested rather than carved.

name: Sasthamcotta Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
deity: Dharma Sastha, with consort Prabha and son Sathyaka
significance: One of the five ancient Sastha temples of Kerala, alongside Sabarimala, Achankovil, Aryankavu and Kulathupuzha, standing on high ground ringed on three sides by the state's largest freshwater lake. Its resident monkeys are treated as sacred and are cared for by a trust fund set up in 1996.
story: Rama is said to have stopped here on his return from Lanka to honour Dharma Sastha, leaving behind Neelan, chief architect of his vanara army, whose descendants are held to be the temple's monkeys.

name: Sikharagiriswara Temple, Kudumiyamalai
significance: A rock temple at Kudumiyanmalai near Pudukkottai carrying inscriptions of the Pallava king Mahendravarman, among them a celebrated treatise on music. Its later complex includes a thousand-pillared hall and mandapas carved as chariots drawn by elephants and horses.

name: Shri Mansa Mata Mandir, Hasampur
significance: A Shakta temple set in a hundred-acre complex in the Hasampur hills near Neem-Ka-Thana, counted among the prominent goddess shrines of north India and thronged during Navratri. It is run by the Shri Mata Mansa Devi Shrine Board constituted under a 1991 Rajasthan act.

name: Shani Dham Temple
significance: A Delhi temple to Shani at Asola, reported to hold the largest rock image of the deity in the world, unveiled on 31 May 2003. Its eastern hall sets the Shani image beside the twelve Jyotirlingas, while the western section adds Shani on buffalo and vulture, Hanuman, an oblation pool and the nine planets.

name: Shree Vishnumurthy Temple
builtDisplay: idol c. 600 years old; shrine rebuilt after 1911
significance: An old Vishnu shrine at Kulai north of Mangalore, found in ruins in the forest around 1911 by the local historian Venkatramana Hebbar and repeatedly renovated since. Its image is reckoned to be about six centuries old.

name: Siddha Vinayaka Temple
significance: A Ganapatya shrine in Ganjam district built around an idol that still sits within the joined trunks of two ficus trees, counted in Odisha's Panchadevata tradition. Around 200,000 pilgrims from Odisha and Andhra Pradesh come for Ganesh Chaturthi.
story: The Gajapati king Purushottama Deva of Puri is said to have found the idol in the hollow of a banyan and a peepal while marching on the Kanchi kingdom, and to have consecrated it on the spot.

name: Siddhivinayak Mahaganapati Temple, Titwala
significance: A much-visited Ganesha temple at Titwala on an ancient site, renovated under Peshwa Madhavrao I and rebuilt in 1965-66, with further work finished in 2009. Devotees come specifically to seek marriages and to settle marital difficulties.
story: Sage Kanva is said to have told Shakuntala, estranged from King Dushyanta, to raise a shrine here to Ganesha as Siddhi Vinayaka.

name: Sita Samahit Sthal
significance: A temple completed in 1990 by Sri Prakash Narayan Punj on the road between Prayagraj and Varanasi, marking the spot where tradition holds Sita returned to the earth. Ram Navami is its principal festival.
story: Living at Valmiki's hermitage, Sita is said to have asked the earth to take her back after her sons Luv and Kush seized Rama's Ashvamedha horse and fought his army.

name: Shyam Kaka Temple
significance: Built in 1845 on the order of Queen Bhagali Devi in memory of her husband, the local ruler Shyam Dev Khinchi, with the chieftain Amara Singh Gurjar installed as first head priest. Damaged in the British period and rebuilt in August 1987, it is now a protected site of the Archaeological Survey of India.
story: A carved panel shows six Arab men at prayer: local lore says visiting Arabs questioned the priest about the sanctity of Mecca and Medina, and he showed them both cities within the temple, whereupon they prayed there.

name: Sekhareswar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Lathanga in Jagatsinghpur district run by a board of trustees, whose Varuni Yatra is described as a thousand years old. Local institutions including a Sanskrit college take their name from the shrine.

name: Kothandaramaswamy Temple
deity: Rama (Kothandaramaswamy), with Lakshmana, Sita, Hanuman and Vibhishana
significance: A Vaishnava shrine 13 km from Rameswaram, counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshethrams, and the only structure at Dhanushkodi left standing by the cyclone of 1964. A proposed alignment of the Sethusamudram canal was dropped because it would have required demolishing it.
story: This is held to be where Vibhishana, Ravana's brother, surrendered to Rama's army, and where Rama afterwards crowned him king of Lanka.

name: Baba Gangeshwarnath Dham
significance: A Shiva temple at Itahara Uparwar in Bhadohi district, built by Shiv Lal Singh with the help of the Kashi Naresh. It stands on a reach where the Ganges runs from west to east.

name: Kusacode Shri Mahadeva Temple
deity: Shiva, in the form of Kiratha Moorthi
significance: A Shiva temple near Thirumala classed as a Major temple by the Travancore Devaswom Board, with an eight-day Thrikkodiyettu festival. On Shivaratri it is among the busiest shrines in Thiruvananthapuram district after Sreekanteshwaram.

name: Sidhhanath Temple, Kharsundi
deity: Siddhanath (Nathbaba), held to be an incarnation of Shiva
significance: A hill shrine at Kharsundi in Sangli district, roughly four and a half centuries old, whose main gathering falls on Chaitra Ashtami. Nathbaba is a widely followed kuladaivat of the surrounding country.
story: Siddhanath is said to have two wives, Jogeshwari who lives at the temple and Zakabai near Neilkarnji, and by the first wife's condition he may visit the second only once in three years; the spring at Gohdapur is said to have opened where his horse struck the ground as he fled a snake set to stop the meeting.

name: Hulimavu Cave Temple
significance: A cave shrine cut into a single rock outcrop off Bannerghatta Road in south Bangalore, reckoned four to five centuries old and administered by the Sri Sri Bala Gangadaraswami Mutt. It holds three consecrated shrines and a meditation mantapa.
story: The saint Sri Ramanand Swamiji is said to have performed tapas in the cave for many years, and his samadhi lies inside it.

name: Shitala Mata Temple, Patna
deity: Shitala Mata, worshipped as a form of Durga
significance: A goddess temple in Patna City regarded as a Shakta pitha and a centre of Durga worship in the old quarter of the Bihar capital.

name: Shri Kalyan Temple, Diggi
significance: An old Vaishnava shrine at Diggi in Tonk district, rebuilt in 1527, and one of Rajasthan's larger pilgrimage centres. Devotees hold the water offered here to cure skin disease.
story: King Digva, struck with leprosy, is said to have recovered his health after recovering an image of Vishnu from the sea and installing it at Diggi, and the god was thereafter called Kalyanji, the benevolent one.

name: Shree Balaji Mandir
style: Built to shilpa, agama and vastu shastra
significance: A Venkateshwara temple at Charkop in Kandivali West that presents itself as the god's second home after Tirupati. Andal, the adopted daughter of Periyalwar, is honoured here through the Tiruppavai during Dhanurmas.

name: Ganpati Temple, Tasgaon
style: South Indian, with a seven-storeyed gopura
significance: Begun in 1779 by Parasuram Bhau Patwardhan, Sar-Senapati to the Peshwa, and finished by his son Appa Patwardhan in 1799, this temple is known for its 29 m gopura and for an idol whose trunk curves to the right. Its 30 ft chariot procession the day after Bhadrapada Chaturthi has run since 1785.

name: Marubai Temple, Matunga
significance: A shrine to Marubai, the traditional gaondevi or village goddess of Matunga, attested since about 1700 and formally constituted as a public trust in 1952. It survived colonial-era road widening at King's Circle when residents resisted moving it from its original site.
story: Locals held that shifting the goddess from her original spot beneath the peepal tree would bring down her wrath, so the temple was never relocated.

name: Panniyur Sri Varahamurthy Temple
deity: Varaha (boar avatar of Vishnu), with Bhumi Devi
significance: A Vaishnava temple in Pattambi taluk whose presiding image is Varaha seated with the earth goddess Bhumi, an unusual dedication in Kerala. It is counted among the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams of the Vaishnava tradition.
story: Temple tradition credits its founding to Parashurama, who is said to have raised Kerala from the sea, and tells of the master carpenter Perumthachan leaving his tools behind here.

name: Maya Devi Temple, Haridwar
deity: Maya Devi (Shakti), with Kali and Kamakhya
significance: An eleventh-century Shakta shrine east of Har ki Pauri, regarded as one of the three principal siddha pithas of Haridwar. Its sanctum holds Maya Devi flanked by Kali and Kamakhya.
story: The site is held to be where the heart and navel of the goddess Sati fell to earth.

name: Cheruvally Devi Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali temple in Cheruvally village, Kanjirappally taluk, some 35 km south-east of Kottayam, reckoned to be at least a thousand years old. A subsidiary Judge Ammavan shrine was added in 1978.
story: The Judge Ammavan shrine honours a Travancore judge who condemned his own innocent nephew and then sought his own execution; his restless spirit is said to have troubled the place until the shrine was raised to appease him.

name: Pandalam Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple about 3 km from Pandalam town, where the deity is worshipped in a benign aspect with Parvati seated on his lap. It is counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala.
story: Tradition holds that Parashurama installed the sanctum image and that the sage Khara Muni consecrated the shrine as one of 108 Shiva temples.

name: Laxminarayan Temple, Therubali
significance: A modern temple built by the Indian Metals and Ferro Alloys company at its Therubali works, about 25 km from the Rayagada district headquarters. Besides Lakshmi Narayana it houses Hanuman, Shiva and the Jagannath triad.

name: Mariamman Temple, Ooty
significance: A hill-station temple beside the Ooty market, unusual in enshrining Mariamman and Kaliamman together, and one of the best-known Hindu shrines of the Nilgiris.
story: Local tradition tells of two divine sisters who came from the north to the market; sheltered under a tree, they vanished in a flash of light, and the townspeople built the temple where it happened.

name: Thrikkandiyur Mahadeva Temple
significance: An old Shiva temple in the Tirur neighbourhood of Malappuram district, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala.
story: Tradition credits Parashurama, the legendary maker of Kerala, with installing the temple's image.

name: Muthuvara Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Muthuvara in Thrissur district that also maintains a separate shrine for Vishnu within the same compound.
story: Tradition holds that Parashurama, the sixth avatar of Vishnu, installed the temple's image.

name: Manikeshwari Temple
significance: The principal Shakti temple of Bhawanipatna, honouring Manikeshwari as the tutelary goddess of the Naga-descended ruling line of Kalahandi, whose worship the article traces back to the 10th century. The present building was begun by Udit Narayan Deo and finished in 1947 under Brajamohan Deo.

name: Paschimesvara Siva Temple
significance: An 8th-century Shaiva shrine of the Bhaumakara period standing on the south-western embankment of Bindusagar tank in the old temple quarter of Bhubaneswar. Locally called the Big Shiva temple, it rises about 18 m and carries a Mahishamardini image among its sculpture.

name: Sri Sai Janmasthan Temple, Pathri
significance: A modern temple at Pathri built between 1994 and 1999 on the site claimed, after field research in the 1970s, to be the birthplace of Sai Baba of Shirdi. The claim remains contested.

name: Thrichattukulam Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shaiva temple on Panavally island beside Vembanad Lake in Alappuzha district, attributed to Chera patronage and reckoned locally to be of great antiquity.

name: Tukreswari Temple
significance: A hilltop Shakta shrine in Goalpara district counted as a Shakta pitha, where a fragment of the goddess Sati is held to have fallen. Its name comes from the Assamese tukura, a piece or fragment.
story: When a grief-maddened Shiva danced the tandava with Sati's charred body, it came apart and its pieces fell across the earth, one of them at this hill.

name: Mausimaa Temple
significance: A temple in the village of Kulada, about 8 km from Bhanjanagar in Ganjam district, whose presiding goddess is Ardhasini, worshipped as the maternal aunt of Jagannath. Its Ratha Yatra brings Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra to the goddess by chariot.

name: Sri Perungaraiyadi Meenda Ayyanar Temple
significance: An Ayyanar shrine on the bank of the Villuni river at Kulamangalam in Alangudi taluk, traced to the 18th century. Its terracotta horse, 37 ft high with forelegs raised, is claimed to be the largest such figure anywhere; the temple was reconsecrated in May 2010.

name: Marundeeswarar Temple
significance: A Shaiva temple on the Bay of Bengal shore at Thiruvanmiyur, whose masonry structure dates to the 9th-century Cholas with later Vijayanagara expansion; inscriptions of Rajendra Chola record 11th-century endowments. Shiva is worshipped here as Marundeeswarar, lord of medicines.
story: Shiva is said to have taught the sage Agastya the healing properties of herbs at this spot, and Valmiki is held to have worshipped here, giving the place its old name Thiruvalmikiyur.

name: Mithranandapuram Vamanamoorthy Temple
significance: A Vaishnava temple at Cherpu in Thrissur district where Vishnu is worshipped in his dwarf incarnation Vamana, with subsidiary shrines to Ganesha, a guru figure and Annapoorneswari.
story: The temple recalls Vamana's asking of King Mahabali for three paces of ground, a lesson against pride; the image is held by tradition to be more than 1,500 years old.

name: Panakkattodil Devi Temple
significance: A goddess temple at Chavara Thekkumbhagom in Kollam district where Durga and Kali are worshipped with equal standing, alongside Ganapathy, Dharma Sastha, Brahma Rakshas and the serpent deities. No documentary evidence fixes its origin.
story: Local tradition says a wandering Brahmin and the carpenter Koyippurathu Nambeesan Aasari raised the shrine together, and that the Brahmin invoked Bhadrakali into it.

name: Panachikkadu Temple
deity: Saraswati (with Vishnu as the original deity)
significance: Kerala's best-known Saraswati shrine, at Panachikkad in Kottayam district, where the goddess of learning is worshipped in a spring-fed sanctum; Vishnu, installed before her, remains the temple's main deity.

name: Veeranimangalam Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Enkakkad in the south of Wadakkancherry taluk, Thrissur district, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala and notable for the strong presence of Narasimha alongside the principal deity.
story: Tradition credits the sage Parashurama with installing the Shiva image here.

name: Mangottu Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A Bhagavathi temple at Athipotta, about 24 km from Palakkad by way of Alathur, whose goddess is regarded as the younger sister of the Parakkattu Bhagavathi of nearby Kavasseri.

name: Mariamman Temple, Valangaiman
significance: A Mariamman temple at Valangaiman in Tiruvarur district, about 9 km from Kumbakonam on the Needamangalam road, where Shiva is also worshipped.

name: Thalikkunu Shiva Temple
significance: One of the oldest temples of Malabar, at Mankavu about 4 km from Kozhikode railway station. Repeatedly attacked and destroyed during Tipu Sultan's campaigns, it was rebuilt by the Zamorin after 1792.

name: Marichi Temple
deity: Durga (worshipped alongside the Mahayana goddess Marici)
significance: A shrine at Ajodhya in Balasore district where a late 11th-century goddess image is worshipped as Durga beside a figure of the Buddhist goddess Marici. The site preserves an unusual mix of tantric, Buddhist and Jain sculpture, including a Buddha in bhumisparsa mudra and a Jain tirthankara.

name: Thrikkariyoor Mahadeva Temple
significance: One of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala, set on the northern bank of the Kothayar at Kothamangalam in a complex of about four acres with two towers and a large tank. Thrikkariyoor is identified with an early capital of the Chera kings.
story: It is held to be the last of the 108 Shiva temples installed by the sage Parasurama.

name: Bhavnath Temple, Mau
significance: A Shiva temple at Mau village near Bhiloda in Gujarat whose age of roughly thirteen centuries is established by an inscription at the site. The precinct also holds a shrine to Avan Rishi, son of the sage Bhrigu, and a sacred reservoir called Bhrigukund.
story: Bathing in the waters of the Bhrigukund reservoir is believed to cure leprosy.

name: Mezhuveli Temple
builtDisplay: early 20th c. (consecrated by Sree Narayana Guru)
significance: A village Shiva temple raised about a century ago by the people of Mezhuveli under the poet and social reformer Muloor S. Padmanabha Panicker, and consecrated by Sree Narayana Guru. It stands on a former forest tract called Tholekavu, traditionally reckoned part of the Pandalam kingdom.

name: Markandeshwar Siva Temple
significance: A small 10th–11th century Kesari-period shrine inside the Kharakhia Vaidyanath precinct at Bhubaneswar, with Mahishamardini as its enshrined image. The structure is now abandoned and decaying, its masonry split by cracks.
story: Tradition holds that the Kesaris raised the temple to mark a visit by the sage Markandeya.

name: Avari Mata Temple
significance: A goddess shrine at Aasawara village in Bhadesar tehsil, Chittorgarh district, drawing pilgrims who come seeking relief from paralysis and polio. A pond and a Hanuman shrine stand behind the main temple.
story: Avari Mata, said to have been born into a Rathore Rajput family, is believed to have the power to heal chronic and otherwise incurable ailments in those who stay at her shrine.

name: Arayoor Sree Mahadevar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Arayoor in southern Thiruvananthapuram district near the Tamil Nadu border, administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board. Subsidiary shrines house Ganesha, Durga, Murugan, Ayyappa and Nagaraja.

name: Pariyanampatta Bhagavathi Temple
significance: One of the largest Devi temples of the old Valluvanad country, at Kattukulam in Palakkad district, where the goddess is regarded as the protectress of fourteen desams. Its Pooram festival in the Malayalam month of Medam is the temple's principal celebration.

name: Navaladi Karuppuswami Temple
significance: A guardian-deity temple at Mohanur in Namakkal district, reckoned between five hundred and a thousand years old, whose deity the local ruler Mohur Pazhayan is said to have consulted before taking decisions. A naval tree and a neem tree in the precinct are themselves objects of worship, and the temple was reconsecrated in June 2018.
story: After the Chera king Senguttuvan worshipped here before marching north, the naval tree beside the shrine withered, and the deity came to be called Navaladian, the one of the naval tree.

name: Parampanthali Sree Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Mullassery in Thrissur district, about 20 km from Thrissur town, counted among the 108 Shiva shrines of Kerala. Mahashivaratri and the temple's own Shashti festival, with kavadi processions and caparisoned elephants, are its main observances.
story: It is believed to be one of the 108 Shiva temples founded by Parashurama.

name: Mariamman Temple, Irukkankudi
significance: A well-known Mariamman temple standing between the Arjuna and Vaippar rivers at Irukkankudi in Virudhunagar district, held to be roughly three centuries old. The sanctum sits beneath a vimana fronted by an artha mandapa and maha mandapa, with further shrines to Vinayaka, Kathavarayan and Karuppusami.
story: A priest carrying a basket of cow dung is said to have declared, under the goddess's influence, that Amman lay in the ground beneath it; the villagers dug and found a Mariamman image, and built the temple over it.

name: Sri Rama Temple, Ramapuram
significance: A temple to Rama at Ramapuram between Malappuram and Perinthalmanna, with subsidiary shrines to Ganapathi, Sastha and Hanuman. It figures in the Naalambalam pilgrimage of Rama-family temples and keeps Rama Navami as its chief festival.

name: Markandeshwar Mahadev Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on the Markanda river at Shahabad Markanda, about 20 km south of Ambala on the Grand Trunk Road, whose present building dates from the early twentieth century. The river takes its name from the sage Markandeya, and the temple walls carry the scene of Shiva overcoming Yama.
story: Markandeya was fated to die at sixteen, but when Yama came for him Shiva burst out in fury and struck the death-god down, later reviving him on condition that the boy live forever.

name: Parshuram Mahadev Temple
significance: A rock-cut cave shrine to Shiva in the Aravalli foothills on the Rajsamand–Pali border, dated to 1005 CE and reached by a climb of some five hundred steps from Sadri. It holds naturally formed figures of Shiva and Ganesha and nine kunds that are said never to run dry.
story: Parashurama, the sixth incarnation of Vishnu, is said to have cut the cave out with his axe and performed severe penance to Shiva here.

name: Tiruvidaivasal Punniyakodiyappar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Tiruvidaivasal in Tiruvarur district counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams, the shrines hymned in the Tevaram. Its Tevaram hymn by Gnanasambandar was recovered only in 1917, which raised the recognised total of such temples to 275.

name: Sree Dandu Mariamman Temple, Bengaluru
significance: A temple in the Shivajinagar quarter of central Bengaluru dedicated to the goddess Mariamman, a form of Shakti. Its gopura is unusual in carrying a statue of Mahatma Gandhi.

name: Avanavanchery Sri Indilayappan Temple
significance: A 13th-century Shiva temple about 3 km from Attingal town in Thiruvananthapuram district, built under Travancore royal patronage and counted among the older temples of Kerala. Sub-shrines house Ganesha, Ayyappan and the naga deities.

name: Champakesvara Siva Temple
significance: A 13th-century laterite Shiva temple at Ambika Sahi in the Old Town of Bhubaneswar, originally laid out as a panchayatana precinct with subsidiary shrines, one of which holds a broken four-armed image of Kartikeya.
story: The lingam is held to be patalaphuta, self-risen from the underworld, and the precinct is said to be the abode of the champa nagas, serpents that harm no one.

name: Chiravarampathukavu Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A goddess temple at Pazhanji near Kunnamkulam in Thrissur district. Its annual festival on the second Sunday of Kumbham is organised by more than thirty-five committees and draws a procession of some seventy-five elephants.

name: Chintaman Ganesh Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple about 7 km south-west of Ujjain across the Kshipra, dating in its present form to the Paramara rule over Malwa in the 11th and 12th centuries. Its image is revered as swayambhu, self-manifested, and the assembly hall is carried on finely carved stone pillars.
story: Local tradition holds that Sita established the shrine during the age of the Ramayana.

name: Kathiramangalam Vana Durga Temple
significance: A Durga temple at Kathiramangalam in Thanjavur district, 25 km from Kumbakonam, whose principal image of the goddess stands six feet high. The installation is ascribed to the sage Agastya and its early worship to the sage Mrikandu.
story: The goddess is said to travel to Kashi each night and return by morning, and to have covered the poet Kambar's house with paddy when heavy rain fell as he composed his Ramayana here.

name: Azhakodi Devi Temple
deity: Bhadrakali (in calm aspect), with the seven mothers and a Shiva lingam
significance: A Devi temple at Thiruthiyad in Kozhikode, known as Arikkodikkavu until it was renamed Azhakodi in 1965, and now run by the Malabar Devaswom Board. Its priests are said to have hidden the image in the temple tank during Tipu Sultan's invasion.
story: The Zamorin is said to have entrusted six of his generals to the shrine along with an image of Bhavani Devi obtained from Gujarati traders, directing them to install it beside the Bhagavathi in the sreekovil.

name: Kharakhia Vaidyanatha Precinct
significance: A Shiva precinct in Bhubaneswar whose lingam stands in a large circular stone yonipitha on a raised platform beneath a pipal tree. It is called Kharakhia because the shrine is open to the sky and the sun falls directly on the lingam all day; an old laterite well stands beside it.

name: Baneshwar Temple, Nasrapur
significance: A Shiva temple in dense forest about 37 km from Pune, built in 1749 by the Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao at a recorded cost of 11,426 rupees, 8 annas and 6 paise. It holds a Portuguese bell of 1683 taken after the Battle of Bassein in 1739, one of several such bells distributed to Maratha temples, and its name joins ban, forest, to Ishwar.

name: Balaji Mandir, Pune
significance: A Venkateswara temple at Pashan in Pune, begun in 1998 under the Sri Ahobila Mutt with the Sri Lakshmi Nrusimha Sabha and consecrated in February 2002 by the mutt's 45th pontiff. It serves as a regional centre for the Sri Vaishnava community in western India.

name: Kattu Narasimhaperumal Temple, Srirangam
significance: A Narasimha temple at Srirangam attributed to the 9th-century Pandya king Vallabadevan. Pillai Lokacharya gave philosophical discourses here in the 12th century, and Manavala Mamunigal took charge of its administration in the 15th at a Pandya ruler's request.
story: The deity is called Varaprasadi, the granter of boons, and the shrine Ekaanthanthaman Koil for the stillness of its precinct.

name: Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple
deity: Shiva as Kirateshwar, lord of the Kiratas
significance: A riverside Shiva temple at Legship in western Sikkim, grown up around a stone lingam found at the site, with subsidiary shrines to Rama and Durga. Bala Chaturdashi and Maha Shivaratri are its principal festivals, and pilgrims come with prayers for children and for health.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared here to Arjuna in the guise of the hunter Kirateshwar and blessed his penance with success in the Mahabharata war.

name: Manakula Vinayagar Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple 400 m from the Bay of Bengal in Puducherry, of considerable antiquity and older than the French settlement. Attempts to destroy it under Dupleix were abandoned in the face of protest; it was renovated in 2015 and owns a golden chariot of 7.5 kg of gold first drawn in 2003.
story: A saint called Thollaikkathu Siddar is said to have received enlightenment from the deity here about three hundred years ago and taken samadhi in the temple, and newborn children are brought to this shrine before any other.

name: Chandika Sthan
significance: A Shakti shrine at Basudevpur about 2 km north-east of Munger, counted among the Shakta pithas and long associated with Karna, king of Anga, who is said to have worshipped Chandi here daily. Pilgrims come to it particularly for relief from diseases of the eye.
story: When Shiva bore Sati's body across the world in grief, her left eye is said to have fallen at Munger, and the goddess is said to have given King Karna gold each day to distribute in charity.

name: Bagnath Temple
significance: The chief temple of Bageshwar, standing at the meeting of the Sarayu and Gomati, its present building completed in 1450 by the Chand ruler Laxmi Chand over a site attested from about the 7th century. Its sculptures range from the 7th to the 16th century, and the Uttarakhand archaeology department took charge of the inscriptions and images of the 8th to 10th centuries in 1996.
story: Shiva is said to have come to this spot in the form of a tiger to bless the sage Markandeya, who worshipped him here.

name: Chennakesava Perumal Temple, Chennai
deity: Vishnu as Chennakesava Perumal, with Chenkamala Valli Thayar
significance: One of the twin temples of old Madras, first built in 1646 on the ground now occupied by the Madras High Court and demolished by the British between 1757 and 1762 during the expansion of Fort St. George. It was rebuilt on Devaraja Mudali Street in George Town by Manali Muthu Krishna Mudaliar, alongside the Chenna Malleeswarar temple.
story: The name of the city of Chennai is popularly traced to these temples, chenna meaning fair in Kannada and Telugu.

name: Kodimoottil Sri Bhadrakaali Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali shrine at Parippally in Kollam district with subsidiary shrines to Shiva, Ganapati and the Navagrahas. Its ten-day March mahotsavam, opened with pongala and closing with the Gajamela elephant procession, draws participants from every community.

name: Chandrasekhara Mahadeva Temple
significance: A nineteenth-century Shiva temple in Patia village on the northern edge of Bhubaneswar, enshrining a lingam set in a circular yoni pitha. Built of laterite and ashlar in the Kalinga idiom, it retains its vimana with a later concrete hall serving as jagamohana.

name: Astasambhu Siva Temples
significance: A group of eight tenth-century Shiva shrines in Bhubaneswar's old town, five of them aligned in a row locally called the Panchu Pandava. Built as small rekha deuls of grey sandstone in dry masonry, they stand between the Godavari and Bindusagar tanks.

name: Khidkaleshwar Mandir
significance: A Shiva temple on the bank of Khidkali Lake near Dombivli in Thane district, whose present structure was probably rebuilt in the seventeenth century. The complex also holds images of Ganesha and Hanuman, with smaller Dattatreya and Hanuman shrines nearby.
story: Local tradition holds that the Pandavas raised the shrine during their forest exile, when Yudhishthira wished to worship Shiva at the spot.

name: Beejamandal
significance: An unfinished and largely ruined temple at Jatkara near Khajuraho, first raised in the eighth century and rebuilt in the later eleventh. At about 34.6 m long its plinth exceeds the Kandariya Mahadeva, making it the largest temple footprint recorded at the site.

name: Badri Narayanan Temple
significance: A Vishnu temple at the entrance to Alagar Koil in Madurai district, where the principal image shows the god seated in meditation flanked by Nara and Narayana. It is modelled on the Badrinath temple of Uttarakhand and keeps daily rituals with monthly devotional singing.
story: By legend Kallalagar halts here on the eve of the Chittirai festival as he travels from Alagar Koil, and so misses his sister's wedding at Vandiyur.

name: Kodikkunnu Bhagavathy Temple
significance: An old Bhagavathy temple at Pallippuram near Pattambi in Palakkad district, where the goddess Bhadrakali is worshipped simply as Amma and shares the shrine with Shiva. It is unusual in opening three sacred entrances, to the north, east and west.
story: Temple tradition traces the goddess to Muthassiar Kavu Bhagavathi and her daughters, one of whom stayed on as the guardian deity of the kanakkan community.

name: Koorainadu Punukeeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the Koranad neighbourhood of Mayiladuthurai, Tamil Nadu, where the god is worshipped as Punukeeswarar with the goddess Santhanayaki. The name preserves the civet-musk (punugu) association that gives the shrine its identity.
story: A civet is said to have found a lingam in a paddy field at Koranad and anointed it with its own fragrant musk, until Shiva appeared and granted the animal a place at Kailash.

name: Sri Chirakkakavu Bhagavathi Temple
builtDisplay: c. 13th c. (said to be 800 years old)
significance: A goddess temple at Thalassery in North Malabar where Kali is worshipped in three aspects as Thrigunaathmika. The structure is held to be at least eight centuries old and its foundation is credited to the Chirakkal raja of the Kolathiri line.
story: The goddess is said to have revealed herself at Vamal with her retinue, in a palace where the river meets the sea, and in the form of a divine fish.

name: Egowri Amman Temple, Vallam
significance: A goddess temple at Vallam, about 12 km from Thanjavur, whose earliest inscription belongs to the fortieth regnal year of the Chola king Parantaka I. Its image of Ambika is two-faced, one countenance fierce and the other serene, and the maha mandapa was added by Sevappa Nayak and Achuthappa Nayak in 1535.
story: The goddess Gowri is said to have ended the tyranny of the asura Thanjasuran by beheading him in his ox form.

name: Parassala Mahadeva Temple
significance: A centuries-old Shiva temple at Parassala near the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border, founded by Mallen Chembakaraman Delava of the Venad royal house and built largely in stone. Its Shiva faces west, a rare orientation in Kerala, and its rites have long admitted worshippers of every community.

name: Sree Maheswara Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Koorkenchery in Thrissur consecrated by the social reformer Narayana Guru in Malayalam Era 1092, with sub-shrines to Parvati, Ganapati, Murugan, Ayyappan, Krishna, Muthappan, Bhadrakali, the Navagrahas and the nagas. Its seven-day Thaipooya Mahotsavam is among the largest festivals around Thrissur after the Pooram.

name: Ahalya Sthan
significance: A temple at Kamtaul in Darbhanga district dedicated to Ahalya, wife of the sage Gautama, built between 1662 and 1682 under Maharaja Chhatra Singh and Maharaja Rudra Singh. It is described as the earliest Ram-Janaki temple in India.
story: The spot is remembered as the place where Ahalya, turned to stone by a curse after Indra's deception, rose again in her own body when Rama came there with Lakshmana and Vishvamitra.

name: Nallur Sundara Varadharaja Perumal Temple
builtDisplay: c. 16th c. (said to be 500 years old)
significance: A Vaishnava temple about five centuries old at Nallur in Tiruvannamalai district, where Vishnu is worshipped as Sundara Varadharaja Perumal with the goddess Sundaravalli Thayar. Garuda stands in worship at the feet of the main image, and Vaikuntha Ekadashi is the chief observance.

name: Kapilesvara Siva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on the south-western edge of Kapilesvara village in old Bhubaneswar, built in the fourteenth century under the Gajapati ruler Kapilendra Deva on a site thought to hold an older shrine. The sanctum enshrines a lingam set in a circular yoni pitha.
story: Local legend calls this the birthplace of Shiva, honoured here as the father of the universe.

name: Sree Maha Ganapathy Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple at Thamarakulam in southern Kerala where Vigneshwara is regarded as the guardian of the whole locality, with further shrines to Dharmasastha, Murugan and Amman. Its principal observance is the Mandala Puja held as Sasthapreethi Samaradhana.

name: Sri Anjaneya Swamy Temple, Shamanur
significance: The village deity's shrine at Shamanur near Davangere, where a roughly six-foot Hanuman image is said to have been installed by Vyasaraja and the site traced back some eight centuries. The old temple was replaced by a Dravidian-style structure inaugurated in March 2000, and a three-day car festival follows ten days after Mahashivaratri.

name: Adisvaraswamy Jain Temple, Thanjavur
builtDisplay: c. 15th c. (said to be 600 years old)
significance: A Jain temple at Karanthattankudi near Thanjavur enshrining the first Tirthankara Rishabhanatha as Adisvaraswamy, with a two-tiered vimana, rajagopura and a sequence of mandapas added about three centuries ago. It is the only temple in Tamil Nadu with a separate shrine for the Jinavani.

name: Kumbakonam Brahma Temple
significance: A Kumbakonam temple whose moolavar is Vishnu as Vedanarayana Perumal, but which is best known for its shrine to Brahma alongside Saraswati, Gayatri and Yoganarasimha. Dedicated Brahma shrines are rare in India, the other well-known one being at Pushkar in Rajasthan.

name: Gondeshwar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Sinnar in Nashik district built under the Seuna (Yadava) dynasty, laid out as a panchayatana with the main shrine ringed by four subsidiary shrines to Surya, Vishnu, Parvati and Ganesha. One of the finest surviving Bhumija-style complexes in Maharashtra, it is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.
story: Local tradition credits its building to Rav Govinda, son of the Gavali chief Rav Singhuni, at a cost of two hundred thousand rupees.

name: Dubba Rajeswara Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Pembatla in Sarangapur mandal, Jagtial district, counted among the oldest and best-known shrines of the old Karimnagar region. Maha Shivaratri is its principal festival, when special buses run from Jagtial to the temple.

name: Kalahasteeswarar Temple, Kumbakonam
significance: A Shiva temple in Kumbakonam where the god is worshipped as Kalahasteeswarar with the goddess Gnanambikai, renovated by Serfoji of Thanjavur. It is one of the twelve Shiva temples tied to the Mahamaham festival held at Kumbakonam once every twelve years, and was reconsecrated in October 2015.

name: Arulmigu Koniamman Temple
significance: The guardian-deity temple of Coimbatore, on the north bank of the Noyyal, built in the eleventh century by descendants of the chieftain Kovan. Its 84-foot gopuram, finished in 2011, is the tallest in the region, and with Perur Pateeswarar it forms the city's pair of historic temples.
story: The city's name is said to descend from Koyamma, the goddess worshipped by the chieftain Kovan, whose name became Koniamma and gave Koyampuththoor its title.

name: Sree Balakrishna Swami Temple, Kuzhuppilly
significance: A Krishna temple in Kuzhuppilly village on Vypeen Island, maintained by the Goud Saraswat Brahmin community, whose idol was consecrated in 1895 and whose present building was completed in 1964. Its interior walls carry an extensive painted Dashavatara cycle, and sub-shrines honour Hanuman, Garuda, Ganapati, Lakshmi, the Navagrahas and Nagaraja.

name: Sree Bhuvaneswary Temple, Valamchuzhy
significance: One of the oldest temples in Pathanamthitta district, standing where the Achankovil river loops around the site on three sides. It is known for the Rudrapongala of the month of Kumbham and for a Padayani custom in which newborn children are presented to the goddess.
story: A devotee is said to have carried a flower from the Kodungallur Bhagavathy temple in which the goddess Bhuvaneswari dwelt, and was inspired to install her at Valamchuzhy.

name: Jalakandeswarar Temple, Vellore
significance: A Shiva temple inside Vellore Fort at the centre of the city, raised in 1550 by the Vijayanagara chieftain Chinna Bommi Reddi during the reign of Sadasiva Raya. It is noted for a nine-tier gopuram, richly carved stone pillars, monolithic sculpture and heavy wooden gates.
story: The lingam is said to have stood self-manifested within a great anthill ringed by standing water, which gave the god his name from jalam, water.

name: Kal Bhairav Temple, Ujjain
significance: The temple of Ujjain's guardian deity Kal Bhairav, on the bank of the Shipra, standing on older remains that yielded Paramara-period images of Shiva, Parvati, Vishnu and Ganesha. The present Maratha-style building with its deepmalika lamp tower is credited to a restoration by Mahadaji Shinde after 1761, and liquor is still offered to the deity as one of the five tantric panchamakara offerings.

name: Kaliyuga Varadaraja Perumal Temple, Kallankurichi
significance: A Vaishnava temple about 10 km from Ariyalur where the object of worship is a pillar rather than an anthropomorphic image. The building is roughly five centuries old and shows Vijayanagara-period Dravidian work, with sculpted pillars filling the ardha mandapa.
story: A cowherd named Maangan is said to have gone looking for a missing pregnant cow, found her newly calved at the spot, and so learned of a wooden pillar of Vishnu there that held great power.

name: Sreenarayanapuram Mahavishnu Temple
significance: An eighteenth-century Vishnu temple at Manakala, about 4 km from Adoor in Pathanamthitta district. It is one of the few Kerala Vishnu temples that keeps the ten-day Dasavatarachartu festival, in which one avatar of Vishnu is worshipped on each day.

name: Lakshmi Narasimha Temple, Antarvedi
significance: A Narasimha temple at Antarvedi in Konaseema district, standing where the Vasishta Godavari meets the Bay of Bengal, with Lakshmi worshipped here as Rajyalakshmi. Begun in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries and recorded as completed in Shalivahana Saka 1745 (1823 CE), its building by Kopanathi Krishnamma is attested by a stone inscription at the site.

name: Masani Amman Temple
significance: A Shakta temple at Anaimalai near Pollachi, in existence before 1000 CE and kept by many families as their kuladevi shrine. Its goddess is unusual in being shown reclining, some 15 feet from head to foot, holding a damaru, a fire bowl, a kumkum bowl and a trident.
story: Local tradition tells of a woman executed for eating from a cruel king's mango grove, whose execution stone came to be worshipped with offerings of ground red chilli.

name: Rajendracholiswarar Temple, Ilaiyankudi
significance: A Shiva temple at Ilaiyankudi in Ramanathapuram district, counted among the Vaippu Sthalams praised in Tamil Saiva devotional verse, with Gnanambikai as the goddess. It is revered as the birthplace of the Nayanar saint Ilayankudi Maranar, and keeps Maha Shivaratri, Kanda Sashti and Karthikai.

name: Sree Venu Gopala Swamy Temple, Purakkad
builtDisplay: c. 17th c. (said to be 400 years old)
significance: One of the oldest Gowda Saraswat Brahmin temples anywhere, raised at Purakkad in Alappuzha district about four hundred years ago by families who left Goa under Portuguese pressure to convert and were granted land by the Raja of Chembakassery. The temple rises about 29 m and keeps Krishna Janmashtami, Kartika Purnima and Navaratri.

name: Seetha Devi Temple
significance: A temple at Pulpally in Wayanad established in the eighteenth century by Pazhassi Raja, who long managed it, and one of very few in Kerala where Sita's sons Lava and Kusha receive worship. Its tank is among the largest in Wayanad and the annual festival falls in the first week of January.
story: It is told that after Rama abandoned her, Sita came to Pulpally and was sheltered by the sage Valmiki, whose ashram is remembered nearby.

name: Someswarar Temple, Kumbakonam
significance: A Shiva temple at Kumbakonam where the god is worshipped as Someswarar with the goddess Somasundari, its present masonry raised by the Nayaks in the sixteenth century behind a five-tier rajagopuram. The shrine is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, sung by the Nayanars in the seventh-century Tevaram.
story: The name is explained by Chandra, the moon, having worshipped Shiva here, and the lingam is held to be swayambhu, self-formed.

name: Somesvara Siva Temple
significance: A living Shiva temple within the Kharakhia Baidyanath precinct in old Bhubaneswar, dated on architectural grounds to the tenth or eleventh century. It pairs a rekha deul vimana with a pidha deul jagamohana and enshrines a lingam in a circular yonipitha, with Shivaratri, Sankranti and Mahavishuva Sankranti observed.

name: Veeramakaliamman Temple, Arantangi
significance: A goddess temple about 2 km from Arantangi in Pudukkottai district, where Veeramakaliamman is enshrined seated, with a vasantha mandapa and maha mandapa and shrines of Vinayaka and Karuppar in front. Four daily pujas are performed and festivals run through the Tamil year.
story: The place, then called Veeravanam, is said to have been visited by the Pandavas during their forest exile, who worshipped the goddess here.

name: Jambukaranyesvarar Temple, Kundalur
significance: A Shiva temple at Kundalur in Tiruvarur district, some 20 km from Kumbakonam, with the lingam worshipped as Jambukaranyesvarar and the goddess as Anandavalli. It is one of the Vaippu Sthalams named in the hymns of the Nayanar Appar.
story: The place is remembered as Jambu Karanyam, where Sita is said to have worshipped and the sage Roma Maharishi performed penance.

name: Suttharathnesvarar Temple, Uttathur
significance: A Shiva shrine near Siruganur in Tiruchirappalli district counted among the Vaippu Sthalams praised in the hymns of the Nayanar saint Appar. For three days in the Tamil month of Masi the sun's rays are said to fall directly on the presiding deity.

name: Arapaleeswarar Temple, Kolli Hills
significance: A Shiva temple in the Kolli Hills of Namakkal district, counted among the Vaippu Sthalams sung by the Nayanar saints Sambandar and Appar. It sits close to the Agaya Gangai waterfall and the caves associated with the Siddhars Korakkar and Kalanginathar.
story: Devotees who tried to cook fish taken from the temple tank are said to have seen the fish come back to life and swim away, which is why the deity is called Arapaleeswarar.

name: Theneeswarar Temple, Vellalore
significance: A Dravidian-style Shiva temple in Vellalore village on the outskirts of Coimbatore, recorded as completed in 1400 CE. It is also known after the goddess as Sivakama Sundari Ambal Samedha Theneeswarar Temple.

name: Thazhoor Bhagavathy Kshetram
significance: A goddess temple on the bank of the Achankovil river in Pathanamthitta district, reckoned about three centuries old and fully reconstructed in 2020. It is known for its Kumbha Pongala offering and for Padayani and kettukazhcha folk performances.
story: Local folklore holds that Thazhoor Bhagavathy is the sister of the goddess of Valamchuzhy.

name: Chaturshringi Temple
significance: A hillside goddess temple on Senapati Bapat Road regarded as a presiding deity of Pune, built during the reign of the Maratha king Shivaji. Around two hundred steps climb to the shrine, and the complex also holds subsidiary shrines and eight small Ashtavinayaka images on neighbouring hillocks.
story: A merchant devotee named Durlabhsheth Pitambardas Mahajan is said to have been told in a dream to dig into a hill northwest of Pune, where he uncovered a self-formed image of the goddess.

name: Gayatri Gyan Mandir, Mahuda
significance: A temple campus near Mahuda Junction in Dhanbad district completed in April 2004 by the local Yuva Mandal, with three shrines and a yagshala. It is administered under the Gayatri Pariwar trusts headquartered at Shantikunj, Haridwar.

name: Lalbaugcha Raja
significance: Mumbai's best-known public Ganesha installation, established on 12 September 1934 by the Koli fishing community and local traders of Lalbaug. Its ten-day Ganesh Chaturthi display draws well over a million visitors a day, and the idol has been sculpted by the Kambli family for more than eight decades.
story: Fishermen and market vendors whose Peru Chawl market closed in 1932 vowed a permanent Ganesha if they were granted a new marketplace, and installed the idol in thanksgiving when they got one.

name: Thakurbari Temple, Gangtok
significance: One of the oldest Hindu temples in Sikkim, built in 1935 on land granted by the Chogyal and expanded into a temple complex between 1945 and 1947. Housing shrines to most major deities, it is the main gathering point for Gangtok's Hindu community, with Maha Shivaratri and Bala Chaturdasi as its chief festivals.

name: Sundaravarada Perumal Temple, Uthiramerur
significance: A Vishnu temple at Uthiramerur in Kanchipuram district raised by the Pallava king Nandivarman II around 750 CE and extended by the Cholas, Pandyas, Sambuvarayas, Vijayanagara rulers and Nayaks. Spread over about two acres behind granite walls, it has a five-tiered rajagopuram and follows Vaikhanasa Agama worship in the Vadakalai tradition.
story: Sundaravarada Perumal is believed to have shown himself here to the Pandava brothers Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva, and the goddess Anandavalli to Draupadi.

name: Kalupur Swaminarayan Mandir
significance: The first temple of the Swaminarayan Sampraday, begun in 1819 and inaugurated on 24 February 1822 at Kalupur in Ahmedabad, and the seat of the NarNarayan Dev Gadi. Its Burma-teak carving mixes Rajasthani and Marathi folk motifs with Mughal and Corinthian elements, and includes panels depicting the 1857 rebellion.

name: Madai Vadukunda Shiva Temple
significance: A medieval Shiva temple on the Madai Para plateau north of Kannur, associated with the Kolathiri kings of the Mushika line who made the nearby port of Madai their headquarters roughly twelve centuries ago. The plateau stands about 150 feet above sea level with wide views over the surrounding coast.
story: Tradition holds the shrine was raised on the southwest corner of Madai Para at the spot where a swayambhu manifestation of Shiva was found.

name: Veerabhadra Temple, Yadur
significance: A Virabhadra temple on the banks of the Krishna at Yadur in Chikodi taluk, Belagavi district, with carved pillars and sculpture and records reaching back to the twelfth century. Its riverside setting left it submerged for a fortnight during the Krishna floods of 2019.

name: Yama Dharmaraja Temple, Thiruchitrambalam
significance: One of the very few Indian temples where Yama, the god of death, is the presiding deity, located at Thiruchitrambalam in Thanjavur district. Its precinct also holds shrines to Chitragupta, Pambatti Siddhar, Ayyanar and Karuppu Sami.
story: Kamadeva is said to have been burnt to ashes by Shiva nearby and restored to life at this spot at Yama's intercession.

name: Vilappuram Bhagavathy Temple
significance: A small goddess temple at Vilappuram near Chathannoor in Kollam district, known locally as the Anandavilasam Bhagavathi Temple. Its compound also houses the Anandavilasam library, a Kerala State Library Council affiliate with some 13,000 books.

name: Kallil Temple
significance: A shrine cut into a huge rock at Methala near Perumbavoor, originally Jain and turned into a Bhagavathi temple in the ninth century, with rock-carved images of the Tirthankaras Parshvanatha and Mahavira alongside Padmavati. Reached by sixty-nine steps and roofed by a single vast boulder, it is a protected monument of the Kerala State Department of Archaeology.
story: A woman of great beauty is said to have been seen playing with stones in the forest and to have vanished into the cave with them, the stone she tossed up becoming the roof of the shrine.

name: Yamai Temple, Aundh
significance: A hilltop goddess temple at Aundh in Satara district that is the family deity of many Marathi households and has twelve major subsidiary shrines across Maharashtra. Its stone deepmala stands about 71 feet, among the tallest in India, and the adjoining Shri Bhavani Museum holds works by Raja Ravi Varma, M. V. Dhurandhar and Henry Moore. In the seventeenth century the priests of Aundh saved the image from invaders by concealing it behind a mosque-like facade.
story: The goddess is said to be named from the Marathi call 'Ye Mai' - come, mother - used by Mahalakshmi, Jyotiba of Kolhapur and Rama, and is regarded as the elder sister of Tulja Bhavani.

name: Thillai Kali Temple, Chidambaram
significance: A Shakta temple on the northern edge of Chidambaram built in the thirteenth century by the Kadava chieftain Kopperunchingan, holding the goddess in both a benign four-faced form and a fierce Kali form. Its thirteen-day Vaikasi Thiruvizha is the principal festival.
story: Kali is said to have lost a dance contest to Shiva at Chidambaram when he performed the urdhva tandava, and to have withdrawn in anger to settle outside the town.

name: Vilwadrinatha Temple
significance: A Vaishnava temple at Thiruvilwamala in Thrissur district counted among the Abhimana Kshetrams, rebuilt in 1883 by the King of Kochi after fires in 1827 and 1861 and now run by the Cochin Devaswom Board. It holds what is described as the only swayambhu image of Rama in Kerala and a rare separate idol of Lakshmana.
story: The sage Amalaka is said to have done penance here, the shrine being founded to release the ghosts of Kshatriyas slain by Parasurama, and the hill's name is traced to a golden vilwa tree believed to stand in a cave beneath it.

name: Thakazhy Sree Dharma Sastha Temple
significance: An east-facing Sastha temple at Thakazhy in Alappuzha district, six kilometres from Ambalappuzha, unusual in having no subsidiary deities. Worship follows Manayathattu tantric rites with five daily pujas, and the temple is known for Valiyenna, a medicinal oil prepared from Othar hill.
story: Parasurama is said to have installed the idol on Othera hill, from where a flood carried it to a farm; an Odiyan who found it gave it to Vilwamangalam Swami, the sage Udhayarkkan consecrated it, and the King of Chembakassery raised the temple around it.

name: Sri Vishweshwara Temple, Yellur
significance: A Shiva temple in Yellur village of Udupi district reckoned more than a thousand years old, serving the surrounding maagane of villages and rededicated after renovation in March 2009. Maha Shivaratri is its chief festival.
story: A Koraga woman cutting firewood is said to have struck the ground and made the earth bleed, revealing the linga; her cry in Tulu, 'Yelluna Ooru', is held to have given the village its name.

name: Swarnapureeswarar Temple, Semponarkoil
significance: A Shiva temple on the Kaveri at Semponarkoil in Mayiladuthurai district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams hymned in the Tevaram by Sambandar and Appar. Its goddess is Suguntha Kundalambikai, and the place also carried the older names Lakshmipuri and Indirapuri.

name: Thanthondreeswarar Temple, Belur
significance: A Shiva temple on the bank of the Vasishta Nadi at Belur in Salem district, dated to the twelfth century and attributed to a Chola king, with the goddess Dharmasamvarthini. Its seven-tier rajagopuram rises about 97 feet and was rebuilt between 1992 and 2002, being consecrated afresh in February 2002; the temple is linked with Kanampulla Nayanar, forty-eighth of the Nayanmars.
story: A pepper merchant called Manickam Chetty is said to have found a self-formed lingam here and to have built the sanctum, thereafter being known as Milagu Chetty.

name: Ayyanthole Karthyayani Temple
significance: One of the 108 Durga temples of Kerala, standing at Ayyanthole in Thrissur city and administered by the Cochin Devaswom Board. It is among the temples that take part in the annual Thrissur Pooram.
story: The goddess is identified with the child of Yashoda who was carried to Mathura in Krishna's place, and who wounded Kamsa's shoulder as he tried to kill her before revealing herself and foretelling his death.

name: Wandoor Siva Temple
significance: An old Shiva temple at Wandoor in Malappuram district, with a large tank in which devotees purify themselves before worship. Maha Shivaratri is its principal festival.

name: Thandayuthapani Temples, Chettikulam
significance: A hill temple complex to Murugan at Chettikulam in Perambalur district, ascribed to a Pandya king named Kulasekhara and reached by 240 steps. Its four-foot swayambhu image is unusual in showing the god with hair and holding a sugarcane marked with eleven divisions, and on the third to fifth days of the Tamil month of Masi the setting sun's rays climb the deity from foot to face.
story: Murugan is said to have been given the sugarcane by his mother Parvati in congratulation for defeating the demons, and to have carried it to this hill.

name: Subarnameru Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on the bank of the Tel river at Sonepur in Subarnapur district, in a town so full of shrines that it is popularly called the second Varanasi. Shivaratri and Kartik Purnima draw thousands of pilgrims.
story: A local tale of a rain of gold coins granted to a devotee is said to have given the town the names Sonepur and Subarnapur, from the word for gold.

name: Thanikkudam Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A goddess temple on the Puzhakkal river at Thanikkudam in Thrissur, run by the Cochin Devaswom Board. It is one of very few temples where the monsoon flood is allowed into the sanctum to submerge the idol, and devotees bathe in the floodwater beside it during that araattu.

name: Sri Venkatesa Perumal Temple, Mondipalayam
significance: A sixteenth-century Vishnu temple in Kongunadu style at Mondipalayam near Avinashi in Tiruppur district, known as Melathiruppathi and treated as a substitute Tirupati by devotees who cannot travel to Tirumala. The self-manifested image is flat-sided with a conical centre, and its Thirukalyana Utsavam is timed to the Tirumala ceremony.
story: A man named Kondamanaicker is said to have noticed his cow letting down milk on a sandhill and, digging there, to have uncovered the image bearing the conch and discus.

name: Sureswari Temple
significance: One of the oldest Shakta shrines of western Odisha, on the left bank of the Tel river south-west of its confluence with the Mahanadi at Sonepur. The goddess has a wide following across the western districts of the state.

name: Mangala Devi Kannagi Temple
significance: An early historic stone temple at 1,337 metres inside the Periyar Tiger Reserve on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border, ascribed to the Chera ruler Chenguttuvan. It opens only once a year for the Chitra Pournami festival, when about 25,000 pilgrims are admitted with the Wildlife Warden's permission, and it stands in territory disputed between the two states.
story: Kannagi, heroine of the Tamil epic Cilappatikaram, is said to have come to this spot after burning down the Pandya capital of Madurai and to have remained here fourteen days.

name: Thumpamon Vadakkumnatha Temple
significance: One of the very few temples with two Murugan sanctums, the northern holding the warrior form and the southern the child form, and one of the two principal Subramanya temples of Pathanamthitta district. It is laid out on the pancha-prakara plan of five enclosures in traditional Kerala style, with Uthrada Maholsavam and Maha Shivaratri as chief festivals.
story: The deity of the second sanctum is said to have been worshipped by Sakthibhadra, author of the drama Ascharyachudamani, whose story links the temple to Shankaracharya.

name: Thattayil Orippurathu Bhagavathi Temple
significance: One of the best-known Bhagavathi temples of central Travancore, at Thattayil near Adoor, reckoned about twelve centuries old and built in traditional Kerala style. Its annual festival features the Thookkam hook-swinging offering, and the precinct holds subsidiary shrines to Ganesha, Krishna, the naga deities, Yogeeshwaran and others.

name: Kainoor Shiva Temple
significance: An east-facing Shiva temple on the bank of the Manali river at Kainoor in Thrissur district, counted among the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala. A large eastern gopuram was added in recent years; Maha Shivaratri in the month of Kumbham is its main festival.
story: Tradition credits the sage Parasurama with installing the deity here as one of the 108 Shiva shrines of Kerala.

name: Viyyoor Shiva Temple
significance: A west-facing Shiva temple on the northern bank of the Puzhakkal river at Viyyoor in Thrissur district, beside the Kodungallur-Shoranur highway. Ganapathi, Sastha, Kali and the serpent deities are worshipped as sub-deities, and Maha Shivaratri is the chief festival.

name: Vimleshwar Temple, Rivona
significance: A Shiva temple at Rivona in Sanguem taluka of Goa whose lingam is held to be swayambhu, with affiliated deities Kamaleshwar, Mahalakshmi, Maruti, Purush and Ravalnath. The Prabhu Dessai family and the Daivajna Brahmin Rivonkar families serve as its mahajans, and Shigmo, Dasara, Kalo, Pindikaotsav and Shivratri are observed.

name: Sukreswar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple built in 1744 by the Ahom king Pramatta Singha on Sukreswar hill above the south bank of the Brahmaputra at Panbazar in Guwahati, holding one of the largest lingams in the region. His successor Rajeswar Singha endowed it further in 1759, and a long stair descends from the shrine to Sukreswar ghat.

name: Palakkavu Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A goddess shrine at Edava, a few kilometres north of Varkala in southern Kerala, described as one of the older Devi temples of the region. Its ten-day Karthika Thirunal Mahothsavam, held in the Malayalam month of Kumbham, is the main annual festival.

name: Sringapuram Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Kodungallur in Thrissur district, standing beside the Kodungallur Kovilakam palace. Maha Shivaratri is its principal festival.

name: Vishahareswara Temple
deity: Shiva as Vishahareswarar, with Prasanna Parvathy
significance: A Shiva temple on the Kudamurutti branch of the Kaveri in Thiruvarur district, counted among the 108 riverside shrines attributed to the Chola king Aditya I. It was extensively restored by Paruthiyur Krishna Sastrigal with a kumbhabhishekam in 1905 and renovated again in 2017.
story: The name means remover of poison: Shiva is said to have healed the Sun here after Rahu poisoned him, and worshippers seek the shrine's protection from snake venom and malefic planets.

name: Madavar Vilagam Vaidyanathar Temple
deity: Shiva as Vaidyanathar, the god of healing, with Sivakami
significance: A Shiva temple a kilometre south of Srivilliputhur, entered through a five-tiered gateway tower within a granite enclosure. Its pillared halls and major shrines were commissioned in the 16th century under Pandya, Vijayanagara and Nayak patronage, and Shiva is venerated here specifically as a healer.
story: Local tradition holds that Thirumalai Nayak, afflicted by persistent stomach pain, was cured after a forty-eight-day stay at the temple and built the Natarajar hall in gratitude.

name: Thalagireeshwarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Talagirisvara, enshrined as a Dharalingam
significance: A Pallava shrine built by Narasimhavarman II on a hillock above the Panamalai lake, its three-tiered vimana closely echoing the Kailasanatha temple, with squatting-lion pillars typical of the dynasty. Its painted panel of the dancing Shiva is among the earliest known representations of Nataraja.

name: Changankulangara Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple near Karunagappally in Kollam district, counted among the 108 Shiva shrines. Maha Shivaratri and Thiruvathira are its chief festivals.

name: Thirumalai Kovil
significance: A hilltop Murugan shrine near Sengottai in the Western Ghats, reached by 625 steps, and one of the Vaippu Sthalam shrines named in the Nayanar hymns. The present temple was funded in the nineteenth century by Thiruvarutchelvar Sivakami Ammaiyar, who sold all her property to pay for it.

name: Nili Chhatri
significance: A Shiva shrine beside the Yamuna near Salimgarh Fort in Old Delhi. The surviving octagonal building, faced in green, blue, yellow and orange encaustic tiles over stone and masonry, is documented as the tomb of Naubat Khan, raised in 1565 during Akbar's reign.
story: Tradition holds that Yudhishthira, eldest of the Pandava brothers, founded the temple here and performed his ceremonial rites at the spot.

name: Ashtamangalam Siva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Karyattukara in Thrissur city, built in Kerala style with east-facing sanctums. Maha Shivaratri, celebrated in the Malayalam month of Kumbha, is its main festival.
story: It is held to be one of the 108 Shiva temples of Kerala consecrated by the sage Parasurama.

name: Velorvattom Sri Mahadeva Temple
deity: Shiva, worshipped in two forms as Thekkanappan and Vadakkanappan
significance: A Shiva temple at Cherthala counted among Kerala's 108 Shiva shrines, and one of very few in the state with two nalambalams and two flagstaffs. Many Kerala families regard it as their ancestral moolasthanam.
story: The temple's Shiva image is said to have been installed by the sage Parasurama himself.

name: Neemach Mata Temple
significance: A goddess shrine set on a hill above Fateh Sagar Lake in Udaipur, its sanctum holding a stone image of Neemach Mata alongside Ganesha and three stone lions. Long reached only by a 900-metre climb, it gained a monocable ropeway in January 2024.

name: O.T.C. Hanuman Temple, Palayam
significance: A Hanuman temple in central Thiruvananthapuram whose image was carried to the city by Travancore cavalry soldiers after the capital moved from Padmanabhapuram in the wake of Marthanda Varma's reign. It first stood on the grounds of an Officers Training Camp, which gave the temple its initials, and is now run by the Travancore Devaswom Board.

name: Oorpazhachi Kavu
deity: Bhagavathy, Sree Oorpazhachi Daivathar and Vettakkorumakan (Kiratha sunu)
significance: A sacred-grove shrine at Edakkad in Kannur district with three principal deities, rebuilt and enlarged between 1845 and 1899 after its images had been moved for safety during Tipu Sultan's campaigns in the 1790s. Hereditary trustees drawn from nine Nambiar families administer it.
story: Temple lore recounts Kali becoming the gentle Gauri through penance, Vishnu appearing in the guise of a hunter to Vettakkorumakan, and Rama coming here to seek relief from the affliction of Shani.

name: Iluppaipattu Neelakandeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Thiruneelakandeswarar (Padikarai Nathar), with Amirthavalli
significance: A Shiva temple on the banks of the Kaveri at Iluppaipattu in Mayiladuthurai district, also known as Tirumannippadikkarai. It is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams praised in the early medieval Tevaram hymns of the Nayanar saint Sundarar.

name: Karaneeswarar Temple, Saidapet
significance: An old Shiva temple next to Saidapet railway station in Chennai, laid out with two prakarams and a seven-tiered gopuram.
story: The temple's origin story has Indra install a linga here and pray to Shiva to lift a curse from the divine cow Kamadhenu, receiving in return the title Gopathi, lord of cows.

name: Omampuliyur Thuyartheertanathar Temple
deity: Shiva as Pranava Vyakrapureeswarar, with Poongodi Nayaki
significance: A Shiva temple on the northern bank of the Kaveri at Omampuliyur in Cuddalore district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams sung by the Nayanars Tirugnanasambandar and Tirunavukkarasar.
story: It is counted among the Nava Puliyur temples said to have been worshipped by the sages Patanjali and Vyaghrapada.

name: Kurumanakkudi Kannayiram Udayar Temple
deity: Shiva as Kannayiram Udayar (Kannayiranathar), with Murugu Valar Kothi Naayaki
significance: A Shiva temple at Kurumanakkudi in Mayiladuthurai district, one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams celebrated in the Tevaram hymns of Tirugnanasambandar.
story: Vishnu in his dwarf form as Vamana is believed to have worshipped Shiva at this spot.

name: Panchavatee Hanuman Temple
significance: A Hanuman temple in the village of Pappanchavadi in Vanur taluk, about nine kilometres from Puducherry, where the deity is worshipped in his five-faced Panchamukha form.

name: Neelamperoor Palli Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A Bhagavathy temple in Neelamperoor village, Alappuzha district, whose presiding form is Vanadurga. It is best known across Kerala for its Padayani festival.

name: Thirukoteeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Thirukodikaval on the northern bank of the Kaveri in Thanjavur district. Its present structure is credited to Sembiyan Mahadevi, mother of Uttama Chola, in 979, while the earliest inscriptions on the site date from about 750 in the Pallava period; the Nayanars Appar and Sambandar sang its praises.

name: Keshav Rai Temple
significance: A Vishnu temple above the Chambal at Keshoraipatan in Bundi district, begun by Raja Ranti Deo in 1250 and finished four generations later by Rao Raja Chattar Sal in 1641. Its pyramidal shikhara, carved walls and Rajasthani canopies enclose a white stone image of Keshavaraiji seated in lotus posture with discus and conch; worship passed over time from the Ramanuja tradition to Pushtimarg.
story: Vishnu is said to have manifested as two images to reward Raja Ranti Deo's devotion, and local belief holds that the Chambal turns back on itself after touching the feet of Keshav Rai.

name: Vekkali Amman Temple
deity: Vekkali Amman, a form of the goddess Kali
